docs/case-studies/issue-1/research-notes/models.md\n    983 .github/workflows/release.yml\n  27093 total\n# Medical neural network research\n\nPublic-domain Python tools for evaluating medical models, estimating hardware\nrequirements, and planning training experiments. The benchmark uses real,\nopenly licensed medical images and documents downloaded at test time.\n\n[![CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/actions/workflows/release.yml)\n[![License: Unlicense](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Unlicense-blue.svg)](https://unlicense.org/)\n\n## Features\n\n- Seven tasks: toy differential diagnosis, DDXPlus interviews, prescription\n  handwriting, printed case histories, chest X-rays, MRI and ultrasound.\n- The same scoring harness for OpenAI-compatible servers and native MLX-VLM\n  on Apple Silicon. Models and datasets are optional downloads.\n- Pinned file hashes, source attribution in reports, and offline cache reuse.\n- Memory and time budgets, plus inference and training resource estimates.\n- [Research plan and evidence](docs/case-studies/issue-1/README.md), including\n  alternatives, architectures, data collection and fine-tuning.\n\nThese are research smoke tests. Small, selected teaching samples do not\nestablish clinical accuracy. MedGemma 27B and UniMedVL have not been measured\nhere; their resource numbers are estimates. See the\n[delivery audit](docs/audit-2026-10-16.md) for remaining work.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml.git\ncd medical-neural-network-ml\npython3 -m venv .venv\nsource .venv/bin/activate\npip install -e '.[dev]'\n\n# No downloads or model required\nmedbench host\nmedbench run --task diagnosis --backend naive-bayes --count 50\npytest\n```\n\nFor **M3 Pro / Apple Silicon**, use the\n[native MLX instructions](docs/apple-silicon.md). They include a tiny Metal\nsmoke test that needs no model, then bounded text and real-image tests.\nThe Linux llama.cpp script downloads Linux x86_64 executables and refuses to\nrun those executables on macOS.\n\nFor Linux CPU inference with MedGemma 4B (about 3.3 GB of model files):\n\n```bash\nbash scripts/medbench-model-run.sh download\nbash scripts/medbench-model-run.sh run\n```\n\nThis downloads models subject to their own terms. Review those terms first.\nReal data are downloaded into a separate cache. List sources before downloading:\n\n```bash\nmedbench sources\nmedbench fetch --task imaging-xray --out .cache/medbench-data\nMEDBENCH_DATA_DIR=.cache/medbench-data medbench run \\\n  --task imaging-xray --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 \\\n  --count 2 --out medbench-reports/imaging-xray.json\n```\n\nA benchmark that runs out of time or evaluates zero items exits with failure.\nReports retain completed answers and indicate whether the run stopped early.\nFor a hard timeout on native MLX, use `scripts/medbench-mlx-run.py`.\n\n## Hardware and workflows\n\n| Workflow | Hardware and resources | Validation |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Unit tests, lint, types, package/docs build | CPU, Python 3.9+; use Python 3.12 on this Mac; no model | Local and hosted CI |\n| Real sample verification | CPU, network, about 60 MB of data | Hash and license checks; no inference |\n| MedGemma 4B CPU smoke | Linux x86_64, hosted 4 vCPU / 16 GB RAM; allow 8 GB free disk for archives, extraction and weights | Measured on GitHub CPU runners |\n| M3 Pro MLX smoke | macOS, native arm64 Python 3.10+; 256 MiB allocation ceiling | Measured on this M3 Pro |\n| MedGemma 4B MLX | 18 GB unified-memory Mac can be sufficient with other apps closed; approximately 3 GB checkpoint plus runtime buffers; dynamic free-memory preflight | Backend implemented; see local evidence and limits |\n| MedGemma 27B Q4 GPU | Linux x86_64, NVIDIA 24 GB VRAM recommended, 32 GB+ host RAM and 50 GB free disk | Workflow available; GPU measurement outstanding |\n| UniMedVL bf16 | Dedicated CUDA host; at least 40 GB VRAM as an initial capacity target, 64 GB+ RAM and 80 GB free disk | Custom upstream runtime integration outstanding |\n| Fine-tuning / training | Dedicated GPU; depends on optimizer, context, batch, image size and sharding | Formula estimates only; measurements outstanding |\n\nThe [hardware guide](docs/hardware-workflows.md) distinguishes measured\nresults, capacity estimates and missing runtime support. A calculator saying\n`fits: true` does not establish that a model/quantization combination is\nimplemented by a runtime. All sizes in calculator output use decimal GB.\n\n```bash\nmedbench estimate --model medgemma-4b-it --hardware m3-pro-18gb --quant Q4_K_M\nmedbench estimate --model medgemma-27b-it --hardware l4-24gb --quant Q4_K_M\nmedbench estimate --model unimedvl --hardware a100-80gb --quant bf16 --finetune\n```\n\nThe optional self-hosted NVIDIA job runs only on manual dispatch:\n\n```bash\ngh workflow run model-tests.yml -f gpu=true -f gpu-model=medgemma-27b-it -f count=20\n```\n\n## Configuration\n\n- `pyproject.toml`: package identity, extras, tests and changelog configuration.\n- `MEDBENCH_DATA_DIR`: cache for separately licensed test files.\n- `MEDBENCH_OFFLINE=1`: refuse data downloads; cached hashes are still checked.\n- `MEDBENCH_API_KEY`: optional API key for a model server.\n- `medbench run --help`: task, backend, token and time limits.\n- [Linux runner configuration](docs/case-studies/issue-1/ci-and-gpu-runner.md).\n\nThe distribution is named `medical-neural-network-ml`; the research module and\nCLI are named `medbench`. The inherited `my_package` arithmetic example is\nretained for compatibility and is not the medical benchmark API.\n\n## Development and documentation\n\n```bash\nruff check .\nruff format --check .\nmypy src/\npython scripts/check_file_size.py\nbash scripts/check-required-docs.sh\npip install -e '.[docs]'\nsphinx-build -W --keep-going -b html docs _site\n```\n\nAPI documentation is generated from `medbench`. For GitHub Pages, set\nSettings → Pages → Source to GitHub Actions and the repository variable\n`DEPLOY_GITHUB_PAGES=true`. Otherwise CI builds the site without deployment.\n[Preview regeneration](docs/preview-regeneration.md) records inherited template\ntracking; there is no browser application in this repository.\n\nPublishing requires a PyPI trusted publisher for this repository and package\nname. See the [delivery audit](docs/audit-2026-10-16.md). CI checks publisher\ncredentials and refuses a release when they are not configured.\n\n## Contributing\n\nSee [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Include a changelog fragment for code\nchanges. New original contributions must remain under the Unlicense. Keep\nthird-party weights and test media in ignored caches, with their licenses\nand attribution attached to any redistributed output.\n\n## License\n\nOriginal code is released into the public domain under the\n[Unlicense](LICENSE). This dedication does not relicense third-party material.\n[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) describes dataset excerpts,\nmodel terms, dependencies and report attribution. Downloaded data can require\nattribution or share-alike terms even though this repository's code is public\ndomain.\n\nThe CI/CD tooling was adapted from the public-domain\n[Python development pipeline template](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template).\n# Contributing to medical-neural-network-ml\n\nThank you for your interest in contributing! This document provides guidelines and instructions for contributing to this project.\n\n## Development Setup\n\n1. **Fork and clone the repository**\n\n   ```bash\n   git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/medical-neural-network-ml.git\n   cd medical-neural-network-ml\n   ```\n\n2. **Create a virtual environment**\n\n   ```bash\n   python -m venv .venv\n   source .venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: .venv\\Scripts\\activate\n   ```\n\n3. **Install dependencies**\n\n   ```bash\n   pip install -e \".[dev]\"\n   ```\n\n4. **Install pre-commit hooks**\n\n   ```bash\n   pip install pre-commit\n   pre-commit install\n   ```\n\n## Development Workflow\n\n1. **Create a feature branch**\n\n   ```bash\n   git checkout -b feature/my-feature\n   ```\n\n2. **Make your changes**\n\n   - Write code following the project's style guidelines\n   - Add tests for any new functionality\n   - Update documentation as needed\n\n3. **Run quality checks**\n\n   ```bash\n   # Lint code\n   ruff check .\n\n   # Format code\n   ruff format .\n\n   # Type check\n   mypy src/\n\n   # Check file sizes\n   python scripts/check_file_size.py\n\n   # Run all checks together\n   ruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy src/ && python scripts/check_file_size.py\n   ```\n\n4. **Run tests**\n\n   ```bash\n   # Run tests\n   pytest\n\n   # Run tests with coverage\n   pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term --cov-report=html\n   ```\n\n   If you changed public APIs or docstrings, build the documentation locally to\n   make sure Sphinx still renders without warnings:\n\n   ```bash\n   pip install -e \".[docs]\"\n   sphinx-build -W --keep-going -b html docs _site\n   ```\n\n5. **Add a changelog fragment**\n\n   For any user-facing changes, create a changelog fragment:\n\n   ```bash\n   # Create a new changelog fragment (similar to `npx changeset` in JS)\n   scriv create\n   ```\n\n   This will create a new file in `changelog.d/`. Edit it to document your changes:\n\n   ```markdown\n   ### Added\n   - Description of new feature\n\n   ### Fixed\n   - Description of bug fix\n   ```\n\n   **Why fragments?** This prevents merge conflicts in CHANGELOG.md when multiple PRs are open simultaneously (same as Changesets in JavaScript).\n\n6. **Commit your changes**\n\n   ```bash\n   git add .\n   git commit -m \"feat: add new feature\"\n   ```\n\n   Pre-commit hooks will automatically run and check your code.\n\n7. **Push and create a Pull Request**\n\n   ```bash\n   git push origin feature/my-feature\n   ```\n\n   Then create a Pull Request on GitHub.\n\n## Code Style Guidelines\n\nThis project uses:\n\n- **Ruff** for linting and formatting (replaces black, isort, flake8)\n- **mypy** for static type checking\n- **pytest** for testing\n\n### Code Standards\n\n- Follow PEP 8 style guidelines\n- Use type hints for all functions and methods\n- Write docstrings for all public APIs (Google style)\n- Keep functions under 50 lines when possible\n- Keep files under 1000 lines\n- Maintain test coverage above 80%\n\n### Docstring Format\n\nUse Google-style docstrings:\n\n```python\ndef example_function(arg1: str, arg2: int) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Brief description of the function.\n\n    Longer description if needed.\n\n    Args:\n        arg1: Description of arg1\n        arg2: Description of arg2\n\n    Returns:\n        Description of return value\n\n    Raises:\n        ValueError: Description of when this is raised\n    \"\"\"\n    pass\n```\n\n## Testing Guidelines\n\n- Write tests for all new features\n- Maintain or improve test coverage\n- Use descriptive test names\n- Organize tests using classes when appropriate\n- Use pytest fixtures for common setup\n\nExample test structure:\n\n```python\nclass TestMyFeature:\n    \"\"\"Tests for my feature.\"\"\"\n\n    def test_basic_functionality(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Test basic functionality.\"\"\"\n        assert my_function() == expected_result\n\n    def test_edge_case(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Test edge case.\"\"\"\n        assert my_function(edge_case_input) == expected_result\n```\n\n## Pull Request Process\n\n1. Ensure all tests pass locally\n2. Update documentation if needed\n3. Add a changelog fragment with `scriv create` (see step 5 in Development Workflow)\n4. Ensure the PR description clearly describes the changes\n5. Link any related issues in the PR description\n6. Wait for CI checks to pass\n7. Address any review feedback\n\n## Changelog Management\n\nThis project uses [Scriv](https://scriv.readthedocs.io/) for changelog management, which works similarly to [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) in JavaScript projects.\n\n### Creating a Fragment\n\n```bash\n# Install scriv (included in dev dependencies)\npip install -e \".[dev]\"\n\n# Create a new fragment\nscriv create\n```\n\n### Fragment Categories\n\nUse these categories in your fragments:\n\n- **Added**: New features\n- **Changed**: Changes to existing functionality\n- **Deprecated**: Features that will be removed in future\n- **Removed**: Features that were removed\n- **Fixed**: Bug fixes\n- **Security**: Security-related changes\n\n### During Release\n\nFragments are automatically collected into CHANGELOG.md during the release process. The release workflow:\n\n1. Bumps the version in pyproject.toml\n2. Collects all fragments with `scriv collect --version` using the new version\n3. Updates CHANGELOG.md and removes processed fragment files\n4. Commits the version and changelog together\n5. Publishes to PyPI\n6. Creates a git tag and GitHub release\n\n## Project Structure\n\n```\n.\n├── .github/workflows/    # GitHub Actions CI/CD\n├── changelog.d/          # Changelog fragments (like .changeset/)\n│   ├── README.md         # Fragment instructions\n│   └── *.md              # Individual changelog fragments\n├── examples/             # Usage examples\n├── scripts/              # Utility scripts\n├── src/medbench/         # Research tools and benchmark code\n│   ├── __init__.py       # Package entry point\n│   └── py.typed          # Type marker file\n├── tests/                # Test files\n├── .pre-commit-config.yaml  # Pre-commit hooks\n├── .ruff.toml            # Ruff configuration\n├── pyproject.toml        # Project configuration\n├── CHANGELOG.md          # Project changelog\n├── CONTRIBUTING.md       # This file\n└── README.md             # Project README\n```\n\n## Release Process\n\nThis project uses semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH):\n\n- **MAJOR**: Breaking changes\n- **MINOR**: New features (backward compatible)\n- **PATCH**: Bug fixes (backward compatible)\n\nReleases are managed through GitHub releases and PyPI publishing is handled via GitHub Actions.\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for bugs or feature requests\n- Use discussions for questions and general help\n- Check existing issues and PRs before creating new ones\n\n## Code of Conduct\n\n- Be respectful and inclusive\n- Provide constructive feedback\n- Focus on what is best for the community\n- Show empathy towards other community members\n\nThank you for contributing!\n\n## Licensing contributions\n\nOriginal contributions are dedicated to the public domain under the Unlicense.\nDo not copy third-party code, datasets or model weights into the source tree\nwithout recording their separate terms in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. estimating hardware\nrequirements, and planning training experiments. The benchmark uses real,\nopenly licensed medical images and documents downloaded at test time.\n\n[![CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/actions/workflows/release.yml)\n[![License: Unlicense](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Unlicense-blue.svg)](https://unlicense.org/)\n\n## Features\n\n- Seven tasks: toy differential diagnosis, DDXPlus interviews, prescription\n  handwriting, printed case histories, chest X-rays, MRI and ultrasound.\n- The same scoring harness for OpenAI-compatible servers and native MLX-VLM\n  on Apple Silicon. Models and datasets are optional downloads.\n- Pinned file hashes, source attribution in reports, and offline cache reuse.\n- Memory and time budgets, plus inference and training resource estimates.\n- [Research plan and evidence](docs/case-studies/issue-1/README.md), including\n  alternatives, architectures, data collection and fine-tuning.\n\nThese are research smoke tests. Small, selected teaching samples do not\nestablish clinical accuracy. MedGemma 27B and UniMedVL have not been measured\nhere; their resource numbers are estimates. See the\n[delivery audit](docs/audit-2026-10-16.md) for remaining work.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml.git\ncd medical-neural-network-ml\npython3 -m venv .venv\nsource .venv/bin/activate\npip install -e '.[dev]'\n\n# No downloads or model required\nmedbench host\nmedbench run --task diagnosis --backend naive-bayes --count 50\npytest\n```\n\nFor **M3 Pro / Apple Silicon**, use the\n[native MLX instructions](docs/apple-silicon.md). They include a tiny Metal\nsmoke test that needs no model, then bounded text and real-image tests.\nThe Linux llama.cpp script downloads Linux x86_64 executables and refuses to\nrun those executables on macOS.\n\nFor Linux CPU inference with MedGemma 4B (about 3.3 GB of model files):\n\n```bash\nbash scripts/medbench-model-run.sh download\nbash scripts/medbench-model-run.sh run\n```\n\nThis downloads models subject to their own terms. Review those terms first.\nReal data are downloaded into a separate cache. List sources before downloading:\n\n```bash\nmedbench sources\nmedbench fetch --task imaging-xray --out .cache/medbench-data\nMEDBENCH_DATA_DIR=.cache/medbench-data medbench run \\\n  --task imaging-xray --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1 \\\n  --count 2 --out medbench-reports/imaging-xray.json\n```\n\nA benchmark that runs out of time or evaluates zero items exits with failure.\nReports retain completed answers and indicate whether the run stopped early.\nFor a hard timeout on native MLX, use `scripts/medbench-mlx-run.py`.\n\n## Hardware and workflows\n\n| Workflow | Hardware and resources | Validation |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Unit tests, lint, types, package/docs build | CPU, Python 3.9+; use Python 3.12 on this Mac; no model | Local and hosted CI |\n| Real sample verification | CPU, network, about 60 MB of data | Hash and license checks; no inference |\n| MedGemma 4B CPU smoke | Linux x86_64, hosted 4 vCPU / 16 GB RAM; allow 8 GB free disk for archives, extraction and weights | Measured on GitHub CPU runners |\n| M3 Pro MLX smoke | macOS, native arm64 Python 3.10+; 256 MiB allocation ceiling | Measured on this M3 Pro |\n| MedGemma 4B MLX | 18 GB unified-memory Mac can be sufficient with other apps closed; approximately 3 GB checkpoint plus runtime buffers; dynamic free-memory preflight | Backend implemented; see local evidence and limits |\n| MedGemma 27B Q4 GPU | Linux x86_64, NVIDIA 24 GB VRAM recommended, 32 GB+ host RAM and 50 GB free disk | Workflow available; GPU measurement outstanding |\n| UniMedVL bf16 | Dedicated CUDA host; at least 40 GB VRAM as an initial capacity target, 64 GB+ RAM and 80 GB free disk | Custom upstream runtime integration outstanding |\n| Fine-tuning / training | Dedicated GPU; depends on optimizer, context, batch, image size and sharding | Formula estimates only; measurements outstanding |\n\nThe [hardware guide](docs/hardware-workflows.md) distinguishes measured\nresults, capacity estimates and missing runtime support. A calculator saying\n`fits: true` does not establish that a model/quantization combination is\nimplemented by a runtime. All sizes in calculator output use decimal GB.\n\n```bash\nmedbench estimate --model medgemma-4b-it --hardware m3-pro-18gb --quant Q4_K_M\nmedbench estimate --model medgemma-27b-it --hardware l4-24gb --quant Q4_K_M\nmedbench estimate --model unimedvl --hardware a100-80gb --quant bf16 --finetune\n```\n\nThe optional self-hosted NVIDIA job runs only on manual dispatch:\n\n```bash\ngh workflow run model-tests.yml -f gpu=true -f gpu-model=medgemma-27b-it -f count=20\n```\n\n## Configuration\n\n- `pyproject.toml`: package identity, extras, tests and changelog configuration.\n- `MEDBENCH_DATA_DIR`: cache for separately licensed test files.\n- `MEDBENCH_OFFLINE=1`: refuse data downloads; cached hashes are still checked.\n- `MEDBENCH_API_KEY`: optional API key for a model server.\n- `medbench run --help`: task, backend, token and time limits.\n- [Linux runner configuration](docs/case-studies/issue-1/ci-and-gpu-runner.md).\n\nThe distribution is named `medical-neural-network-ml`; the research module and\nCLI are named `medbench`. The inherited `my_package` arithmetic example is\nretained for compatibility and is not the medical benchmark API.\n\n## Development and documentation\n\n```bash\nruff check .\nruff format --check .\nmypy src/\npython scripts/check_file_size.py\nbash scripts/check-required-docs.sh\npip install -e '.[docs]'\nsphinx-build -W --keep-going -b html docs _site\n```\n\nAPI documentation is generated from `medbench`. This document provides guidelines and instructions for contributing to this project.\n\n## Development Setup\n\n1. **Fork and clone the repository**\n\n   ```bash\n   git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/medical-neural-network-ml.git\n   cd medical-neural-network-ml\n   ```\n\n2. **Create a virtual environment**\n\n   ```bash\n   python -m venv .venv\n   source .venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: .venv\\Scripts\\activate\n   ```\n\n3. **Install dependencies**\n\n   ```bash\n   pip install -e \".[dev]\"\n   ```\n\n4. **Install pre-commit hooks**\n\n   ```bash\n   pip install pre-commit\n   pre-commit install\n   ```\n\n## Development Workflow\n\n1. **Create a feature branch**\n\n   ```bash\n   git checkout -b feature/my-feature\n   ```\n\n2. **Make your changes**\n\n   - Write code following the project's style guidelines\n   - Add tests for any new functionality\n   - Update documentation as needed\n\n3. **Run quality checks**\n\n   ```bash\n   # Lint code\n   ruff check .\n\n   # Format code\n   ruff format .\n\n   # Type check\n   mypy src/\n\n   # Check file sizes\n   python scripts/check_file_size.py\n\n   # Run all checks together\n   ruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy src/ && python scripts/check_file_size.py\n   ```\n\n4. **Run tests**\n\n   ```bash\n   # Run tests\n   pytest\n\n   # Run tests with coverage\n   pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term --cov-report=html\n   ```\n\n   If you changed public APIs or docstrings, build the documentation locally to\n   make sure Sphinx still renders without warnings:\n\n   ```bash\n   pip install -e \".[docs]\"\n   sphinx-build -W --keep-going -b html docs _site\n   ```\n\n5. **Add a changelog fragment**\n\n   For any user-facing changes, create a changelog fragment:\n\n   ```bash\n   # Create a new changelog fragment (similar to `npx changeset` in JS)\n   scriv create\n   ```\n\n   This will create a new file in `changelog.d/`. Edit it to document your changes:\n\n   ```markdown\n   ### Added\n   - Description of new feature\n\n   ### Fixed\n   - Description of bug fix\n   ```\n\n   **Why fragments?** This prevents merge conflicts in CHANGELOG.md when multiple PRs are open simultaneously (same as Changesets in JavaScript).\n\n6. **Commit your changes**\n\n   ```bash\n   git add .\n   git commit -m \"feat: add new feature\"\n   ```\n\n   Pre-commit hooks will automatically run and check your code.\n\n7. **Push and create a Pull Request**\n\n   ```bash\n   git push origin feature/my-feature\n   ```\n\n   Then create a Pull Request on GitHub.\n\n## Code Style Guidelines\n\nThis project uses:\n\n- **Ruff** for linting and formatting (replaces black, isort, flake8)\n- **mypy** for static type checking\n- **pytest** for testing\n\n### Code Standards\n\n- Follow PEP 8 style guidelines\n- Use type hints for all functions and methods\n- Write docstrings for all public APIs (Google style)\n- Keep functions under 50 lines when possible\n- Keep files under 1000 lines\n- Maintain test coverage above 80%\n\n### Docstring Format\n\nUse Google-style docstrings:\n\n```python\ndef example_function(arg1: str, arg2: int) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Brief description of the function.\n\n    Longer description if needed.\n\n    Args:\n        arg1: Description of arg1\n        arg2: Description of arg2\n\n    Returns:\n        Description of return value\n\n    Raises:\n        ValueError: Description of when this is raised\n    \"\"\"\n    pass\n```\n\n## Testing Guidelines\n\n- Write tests for all new features\n- Maintain or improve test coverage\n- Use descriptive test names\n- Organize tests using classes when appropriate\n- Use pytest fixtures for common setup\n\nExample test structure:\n\n```python\nclass TestMyFeature:\n    \"\"\"Tests for my feature.\"\"\"\n\n    def test_basic_functionality(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Test basic functionality.\"\"\"\n        assert my_function() == expected_result\n\n    def test_edge_case(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Test edge case.\"\"\"\n        assert my_function(edge_case_input) == expected_result\n```\n\n## Pull Request Process\n\n1. Ensure all tests pass locally\n2. Update documentation if needed\n3. Add a changelog fragment with `scriv create` (see step 5 in Development Workflow)\n4. Ensure the PR description clearly describes the changes\n5. Link any related issues in the PR description\n6. Wait for CI checks to pass\n7. Address any review feedback\n\n## Changelog Management\n\nThis project uses [Scriv](https://scriv.readthedocs.io/) for changelog management, which works similarly to [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) in JavaScript projects.\n\n### Creating a Fragment\n\n```bash\n# Install scriv (included in dev dependencies)\npip install -e \".[dev]\"\n\n# Create a new fragment\nscriv create\n```\n\n### Fragment Categories\n\nUse these categories in your fragments:\n\n- **Added**: New features\n- **Changed**: Changes to existing functionality\n- **Deprecated**: Features that will be removed in future\n- **Removed**: Features that were removed\n- **Fixed**: Bug fixes\n- **Security**: Security-related changes\n\n### During Release\n\nFragments are automatically collected into CHANGELOG.md during the release process. The release workflow:\n\n1. Bumps the version in pyproject.toml\n2. Collects all fragments with `scriv collect --version` using the new version\n3. Updates CHANGELOG.md and removes processed fragment files\n4. Commits the version and changelog together\n5. Publishes to PyPI\n6. Creates a git tag and GitHub release\n\n## Project Structure\n\n```\n.\n├── .github/workflows/    # GitHub Actions CI/CD\n├── changelog.d/          # Changelog fragments (like .changeset/)\n│   ├── README.md         # Fragment instructions\n│   └── *.md              # Individual changelog fragments\n├── examples/             # Usage examples\n├── scripts/              # Utility scripts\n├── src/medbench/         # Research tools and benchmark code\n│   ├── __init__.py       # Package entry point\n│   └── py.typed          # Type marker file\n├── tests/                # Test files\n├── .pre-commit-config.yaml  # Pre-commit hooks\n├── .ruff.toml            # Ruff configuration\n├── pyproject.toml        # Project configuration\n├── CHANGELOG.md          # Project changelog\n├── CONTRIBUTING.md       # This file\n└── README.md             # Project README\n```\n\n## Release Process\n\nThis project uses semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH):\n\n- **MAJOR**: Breaking changes\n- **MINOR**: New features (backward compatible)\n- **PATCH**: Bug fixes (backward compatible)\n\nReleases are managed through GitHub releases and PyPI publishing is handled via GitHub Actions.\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for bugs or feature requests\n- Use discussions for questions and general help\n- Check existing issues and PRs before creating new ones\n\n## Code of Conduct\n\n- Be respectful and inclusive\n- Provide constructive feedback\n- Focus on what is best for the community\n- Show empathy towards other community members\n\nThank you for contributing!\n\n## Licensing contributions\n\nOriginal contributions are dedicated to the public domain under the Unlicense.\nDo not copy third-party code, datasets or model weights into the source tree\nwithout recording their separate terms in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Sequence[object]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Minimum number of insertions, deletions and substitutions from a to b.\"\"\"\n    if len(a) < len(b):\n        a, b = b, a\n    previous = list(range(len(b) + len(truths)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BinaryCounts:\n    \"\"\"Confusion counts for a yes/no question.\"\"\"\n\n    true_positive: int\n    false_positive: int\n    true_negative: int\n    false_negative: int\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_predictions(\n        cls, truths: Sequence[bool], predictions: Sequence[bool]\n    ) -> BinaryCounts:\n        \"\"\"Count agreements between truths and predictions.\"\"\"\n        pairs = list(zip(truths, predictions))\n        return cls(\n            true_positive=sum(t and p for t, p in pairs),\n            false_positive=sum((not t) sensitivity(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Share of sick cases found (recall). Missing disease is costly.\"\"\"\n        positives = self.true_positive + self.false_negative\n        return self.true_positive / positives if positives else 0.0\n\n    @property\n    def specificity(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Share of healthy cases correctly called healthy.\"\"\"\n        negatives = self.true_negative + self.false_positive\n        return self.true_negative / negatives if negatives else 0.0\n\n    @property\n    def accuracy(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Share of all answers that are right.\"\"\"\n        total = (\n            self.true_positive\n            + self.false_positive\n            + self.true_negative\n            + self.false_negative\n        )\n        return (self.true_positive + self.true_negative) / total if total else 0.0\n\n\ndef auroc(truths: Sequence[bool], scores: Sequence[float]) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Area under the ROC curve: chance that a sick case scores above a healthy one.\n\n    Ties count as one half. Returns 0.5 when one of the classes is missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    positives = [s for t, s in zip(truths, scores) if t]\n    negatives = [s for t, s in zip(truths, scores) if not t]\n    if not positives or not negatives:\n        return 0.5\n    wins = 0.0\n    for p in positives:\n        for n in negatives:\n            wins += 1.0 if p > n else 0.5 if p == n else 0.0\n    return wins / (len(positives) * len(negatives))\n\n\ndef _overlap(\n    a: Sequence[Sequence[int]], b: Sequence[Sequence[int]]\n) -> tuple[int, int, int]:\n    inter = size_a = size_b = 0\n    for row_a, row_b in zip(a, b):\n        for x, y in zip(row_a, row_b):\n            inter += bool(x and y)\n            size_a += bool(x)\n            size_b += bool(y)\n    return inter, size_a, size_b\n\n\ndef dice(a: Sequence[Sequence[int]], b: Sequence[Sequence[int]]) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Dice overlap of two binary masks (1 when both are empty).\"\"\"\n    inter, size_a, size_b = _overlap(a, b)\n    if size_a + size_b == 0:\n        return 1.0\n    return 2 * inter / (size_a + size_b)\n\n\ndef iou(a: Sequence[Sequence[int]], b: Sequence[Sequence[int]]) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Intersection over union of two binary masks (1 when both are empty).\"\"\"\n    inter, size_a, size_b = _overlap(a, b)\n    union = size_a + size_b - inter\n    return inter / union if union else 1.0\n\n\ndef expected_calibration_error(\n    confidences: Sequence[float],\n    correct: Sequence[bool],\n    bins: int = 10,\n) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Gap between stated confidence and real accuracy, averaged over bins.\n\n    A model that says \"90% sure\" should be right 9 times out of 10. ECE is 0\n    for a perfectly calibrated model.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not confidences:\n        return 0.0\n    totals = [0] * bins\n    confidence_sums = [0.0] * bins\n    correct_sums = [0] * bins\n    for confidence, is_correct in zip(confidences, correct):\n        index = min(bins - 1, int(confidence * bins))\n        totals[index] += 1\n        confidence_sums[index] += confidence\n        correct_sums[index] += bool(is_correct)\n    error = 0.0\n    for total, conf_sum, corr_sum in zip(totals, confidence_sums, correct_sums):\n        if total:\n            error += total / len(confidences) * abs(conf_sum / total - corr_sum / total)\n    return error\n\n\ndef bootstrap_ci(\n    values: Sequence[float],\n    confidence: float = 0.95,\n    resamples: int = 1000,\n    seed: int = 0,\n) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Confidence interval of the mean by resampling with replacement.\n\n    With few test cases a score is very uncertain; reporting the interval\n    keeps us from celebrating noise.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not values:\n        return (0.0, 0.0)\n    rng = random.Random(seed)\n    n = len(values)\n    means = sorted(sum(rng.choices(values, k=n)) / n for _ in range(resamples))\n    low = means[int((1 - confidence) / 2 * resamples)]\n    high = means[min(resamples - 1, int((1 + confidence) / 2 * resamples))]\n    return (low, high)",

Sequence[object]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Minimum number of insertions, deletions and substitutions from a to b.\"\"\"\n    if len(a) < len(b):\n        a, b = b, a\n    previous = list(range(len(b) + len(truths)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BinaryCounts:\n    \"\"\"Confusion counts for a yes/no question.\"\"\"\n\n    true_positive: int\n    false_positive: int\n    true_negative: int\n    false_negative: int\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_predictions(\n        cls, truths: Sequence[bool], predictions: Sequence[bool]\n    ) -> BinaryCounts:\n        \"\"\"Count agreements between truths and predictions.\"\"\"\n        pairs = list(zip(truths, predictions))\n        return cls(\n            true_positive=sum(t and p for t, p in pairs),\n            false_positive=sum((not t) Returns 0.5 when one of the classes is missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    positives = [s for t, s in zip(truths, scores) if t]\n    negatives = [s for t, s in zip(truths, scores) if not t]\n    if not positives or not negatives:\n        return 0.5\n    wins = 0.0\n    for p in positives:\n        for n in negatives:\n            wins += 1.0 if p > n else 0.5 if p == n else 0.0\n    return wins / (len(positives) * len(negatives))\n\n\ndef _overlap(\n    a: Sequence[Sequence[int]], b: Sequence[Sequence[int]]\n) -> tuple[int, int, int]:\n    inter = size_a = size_b = 0\n    for row_a, row_b in zip(a, b):\n        for x, y in zip(row_a, row_b):\n            inter += bool(x and y)\n            size_a += bool(x)\n            size_b += bool(y)\n    return inter, size_a, size_b\n\n\ndef dice(a: Sequence[Sequence[int]], b: Sequence[Sequence[int]]) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Dice overlap of two binary masks (1 when both are empty).\"\"\"\n    inter, size_a, size_b = _overlap(a, b)\n    if size_a + size_b == 0:\n        return 1.0\n    return 2 * inter / (size_a + size_b)\n\n\ndef iou(a: Sequence[Sequence[int]], b: Sequence[Sequence[int]]) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Intersection over union of two binary masks (1 when both are empty).\"\"\"\n    inter, size_a, size_b = _overlap(a, b)\n    union = size_a + size_b - inter\n    return inter / union if union else 1.0\n\n\ndef expected_calibration_error(\n    confidences: Sequence[float],\n    correct: Sequence[bool],\n    bins: int = 10,\n) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Gap between stated confidence and real accuracy, averaged over bins.\n\n    A model that says \"90% sure\" should be right 9 times out of 10. For a definitive answer, check GitHub's current documentation on rulesets and the bypass list, or test with a personal repo and a GitHub App.\n\n\nREMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks."

The imports are `data.*` and `modeling.*`, so `ROOT` has to point at the `codes/` directory.\n- **L58–71, `DEFAULT_CONFIG`:**\n  - `\"max_mem_per_gpu\": \"40GiB\"`, `\"temperature\": 1.0`, `\"max_new_tokens\": [REDACTED], `\"do_sample\": True`, `\"seed\": 42`\n  - `\"enable_cpu_loading\": True`, `\"enable_auto_bf16_conversion\": True`\n  - `\"use_model_checkpoint\": False  # False = ema.safetensors`, `\"offload_folder\": \"/tmp/bagel_offload\"` (the offload folder is never used)\n- **Model build, L206–228:**\n  - L206–209 read `llm_config.json` and set `qk_norm=True`, `tie_word_embeddings=False`, `layer_module=\"Qwen2MoTDecoderLayer\"`.\n  - L211–213 read `vit_config.json`, set `rope=False`, and do `vit_config.num_hidden_layers = vit_config.num_hidden_layers - 1`.\n  - L215–222: `BagelConfig(visual_gen=False, visual_und=True, ..., vit_max_num_patch_per_side=70, connector_act='gelu_pytorch_tanh')`.\n  - The model is built under `init_empty_weights()` as `Bagel(Qwen2ForCausalLM, SiglipVisionModel, config)`, then `convert_conv2d_to_linear(vit_config, meta=True)`.\n  - Tokenizer: `Qw…h)` plus `add_special_tokens`, which adds `<|im_start|>`/`<|im_end|>` (used as BOS/EOS) and the vision tokens.\n- **Weight loading, L134–156:** it prefers `ema_bf16.safetensors`, then `load_checkpoint_and_dispatch(..., device_map=<all cpu>, dtype=torch.bfloat16)`.\n- **GPU placement, L167–187:**\n  - With one GPU: `infer_auto_device_map(max_memory={0: max_mem_per_gpu}, no_split_module_classes=[\"Bagel\",\"Qwen2MoTDecoderLayer\"])`, keeping embed_tokens, connector and vit_pos_embed on the same device, then `dispatch_model`.\n  - With several GPUs: everything goes to `target_device`.\n- **Inference, L308–321:** `process_conversation([PIL image], prompt)` only converts to RGB. Then:\n  `self.model.chat(self.tokenizer, self.new_token_ids, self.image_transform, images=images, prompt=conversation, max_length=max_new_tokens, do_sample=do_sample, temperature=temperature)`\n  The demo cell uses `temperature=0.1, max_new_tokens=[REDACTED] There is no think mode on this path.\n- **`Bagel.chat` (`bagel.py` L1321–1392):** prefills the ViT image into a `NaiveCache`, then the text wrapped as `[im_start] + tokens + [im_end]`, then `generate_text` under bf16 autocast. The output is split on `<|im_end|>`/`<|im_start|>`. It handles one image and one turn, with no system prompt.\n- **Think mode** exists only in `codes/inferencer.py`: `InterleaveInferencer.interleave_inference(think=False, max_think_token_n=[REDACTED], ...)` with `VLM_THINK_SYSTEM_PROMPT` at L23.\n- **Gotcha:** `build_transform()` (`eval/vlm/utils.py:486`) opens the relative path `\"codes/data/default.yaml\"`, so the working directory must be the repo root. It uses the `vlm_sft` settings: stride 14, max 980, min 378, max_pixels 2,007,040.\n\n## 4. Hugging Face checkpoint\n- **Repo:** `General-Medical-AI/UniMedVL`, sha `29918cef3ce94a13fe1670145c32a3d1198aec7d`, lastModified 2026-02-10. License `apache-2.0`; `gated: false`.\n- **Files that matter:**\n  - `ema_bf16.safetensors`: 29,214,685,336 B (LFS sha256 `254873338061b90aefa2ec89fa07e4a50ede812c84dd72a83a13fd7db2237b18`)\n  - `ae.safetensors`: 335,304,388 B (sha256 `afc8e282…529e38`; only needed for image generation)\n  - Configs and tokenizer: `co…on`, `llm_config.json`, `vit_config.json`, `tokenizer.json`, `tokenizer_config.json`, `vocab.json`, `merges.txt`\n  - Everything else is images and the README.\n- **Safetensors total:** 29,549,989,724 B (about 27.5 GiB).\n- **From the header:** 1,223 tensors, all BF16, 14,607,260,128 parameters. The LLM has 28 layers, including the `*_moe_gen` MoT experts. The ViT has 26 layers (0–25).\n- **No GGUF, quantized, or fine-tuned variants exist.** A search for UniMedVL returns only this repo, and the `base_model:quantized/finetune/adapter` filters are empty.\n- **`trust_remote_code` will not work:** `config.json` `auto_map` points to `modeling_unimedvl.UniMedVL`, but that file is not in the repo. Use the GitHub code instead.\n\n## 5. Base model and license\n- **Base:** BAGEL (https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Bagel, Apache-2.0, no NOTICE file). HF `ByteDance-Seed/BAGEL-7B-MoT` lists `base_model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct`. The vision encoder is SigLIP: 1152 hidden, patch 14, 980px.\n- **Headers to keep:** `qwen2_navit.py` carries the copyright lines \"The Qwen Team and The HuggingFace Inc. team\", \"Bytedance Ltd.\", and \"Unimedvl Team\", plus a \"modified by ByteDance … 2025-05-20\" note.\n- **What Apache-2.0 §4 requires:** ship the license text, keep those headers, and mark any files you modify. No NOTICE file needs to be carried over.\n\n## 6. GPU memory\n- **No official requirement or tested-GPU list** exists in the UniMedVL README or model card.\n- The only number is the script default `max_mem_per_gpu: \"40GiB\"`. The bf16 weights alone are about 27.2 GiB, so at least 40 GB of VRAM (A100-40G or better) is a reasonable inference.\n- Upstream BAGEL's README suggests 32 GB+ VRAM for full precision, or NF4/INT8 quantization for 12–32 GB. Those figures are for BAGEL, not UniMedVL.\n\n## Caveat (issue #5)\nhttps://github.com/uni-medical/UniMedVL/issues/5 reported that ViT layer-25 weights in `ema_bf16.safetensors` were \"not used\". The maintainer said it was fixed, and a commenter pointed at the `- 1` line. That line is still at L213 in HEAD, and the HF `vit_config.json` says 26 layers while the checkpoint holds 26. So the script as written builds a 25-layer ViT and drops the last layer. Your adapter should probably not subtract 1.\n\n**Sources:**\n- https://github.com/uni-medical/UniMedVL/tree/f51aa0accbd02e846e5ea20b595fb39b516dbe1f\n- https://huggingface.co/api/models/General-Medical-AI/UniMedVL\n- https://huggingface.co/General-Medical-AI/UniMedVL/tree/29918cef3ce94a13fe1670145c32a3d1198aec7d\n- https://huggingface.co/api/models/ByteDance-Seed/BAGEL-7B-MoT",

1.025.274Z\"></path></svg>\n164:Defines a **cooldown period** for dependency updates, allowing updates to be delayed for a configurable number of days. The `cooldown` option is only available for *version* updates, not *security* updates.\n166:This feature enables users to customize how often Dependabot generates new version updates, offering greater control over update frequency. For examples, see [Optimizing the creation of pull requests for Dependabot version updates](/en/code-security/tutorials/secure-your-dependencies/optimizing-pr-creation-version-updates#setting-up-a-cooldown-period-for-dependency-updates).\n171:* Apply a **default cooldown period of 3 days** to version updates, even when `cooldown` is not configured. A new version is not considered for a version update until 3 days after its release. **This default cooldown does not apply to security updates.**\n173:You can configure the `cooldown` option to customize these default cooldown periods and control which dependencies they apply to. When **`cooldown`** is defined:\n176:2. Dependabot checks for any cooldown settings.\n177:3. If a dependency’s new release falls within its cooldown period, Dependabot skips updating the version for that dependency.\n178:4. Dependencies without a cooldown period, or those past their cooldown period, are updated to the latest version as per the configured `versioning-strategy` setting.\n179:5. After a cooldown ends for a dependency, Dependabot resumes updating the dependency following the standard update strategy defined in `dependabot.yml`.\n181:### **Configuration of `cooldown`**\n183:You can specify the duration of the cooldown using the options below.\n187:| `default-days`      | **Default cooldown period for dependencies** without specific rules (optional). If not specified, Dependabot applies a default cooldown of 3 days. |\n188:| `semver-major-days` | Cooldown period for **major version updates** (optional, applies only to package managers supporting SemVer).                                      |\n189:| `semver-minor-days` | Cooldown period for **minor version updates** (optional, applies only to package managers supporting SemVer).                                      |\n190:| `semver-patch-days` | Cooldown period for **patch version updates** (optional, applies only to package managers supporting SemVer).                                      |\n191:| `include`           | List of dependencies to **apply cooldown** (up to **150 items**). |\n123:Dependabot can add metadata from Docker images to pull requests for version updates. The metadata includes release notes, changelogs and the commit history. Repository administrators can use the metadata to quickly evaluate the stability risk of the dependency update.\n141:* Dependabot only supports updates to GitHub Actions using the GitHub repository syntax, such as `actions/checkout@v6` or `actions/checkout@<commit>` . Dependabot will ignore actions or reusable workflows referenced locally (for example, `./.github/actions/foo.yml`).\n142:* Dependabot updates the version documentation of GitHub Actions when the comment is on the same line, such as `actions/checkout@<commit> #<tag or link>` or `actions/checkout@<tag> #<tag or link>`.\n143:* If the commit you use is not associated with any tag, Dependabot will update the GitHub Actions to the latest commit (which might differ from the latest release).\n190:Dependabot monitors your `flake.lock` file and opens pull requests when newer commits are available upstream for your flake inputs. GitHub, GitLab, SourceHut, and plain Git inputs are all supported. Updating pinned refs inside `flake.nix` itself (for example, changing `github:cachix/devenv/v0.5` to a newer tag) is not supported.\n208:### pre-commit\n210:Dependabot can update hook revisions in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` files. Get started How Runpod pricing works Runpod pricing is based on the type of GPU workload you run. Pods are dedicated GPU instances for development and long-running jobs, Serverless bills inference workers based on usage, and Clusters support multi-node workloads and reserved capacity. Storage and deployment choices affect total cost, so teams should choose the model that matches workload duration, traffic pattern, and control needs. All sources were accessed 2026-10-16.\n\n## A. GitHub rulesets\n\n**A1. REST schema** (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules)\n- **Bypass actor types:** `Integration`, `OrganizationAdmin`, `RepositoryRole`, `Team`, `DeployKey`, `User`.\n- **Bypass modes:** `always` (the default), `pull_request`, `exempt`.\n  - \"OrganizationAdmin is not applicable for personal repositories.\"\n  - \"If actor_type is DeployKey, this should be null.\"\n  - \"pull_request is only applicable to branch rulesets. When bypass_mode is exempt, rules will not be run for that actor and a bypass audit entry will not be created.\" Exempt mode was added on 2025-09-10 (https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-10-github-ruleset-exemptions-and-repository-insights-updates/).\n- **Branch conditions:** `include` \"Also accepts ~DEFAULT_BRANCH … or ~ALL\". `enforcement` is disabled, active or evaluate; evaluate is Enterprise only.\n- **Rules with no parameters:** `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`, `required_linear_history`.\n- **`pull_request` parameters:** `required_approving_review_count`, `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push`, `require_code_owner_review`, `require_last_push_approval`, `required_review_thread_resolution`, `allowed_merge_methods` (merge, squash, rebase).\n- **`required_status_checks` parameters:** `strict_required_status_checks_policy` (\"must be tested with the latest code\"), `do_not_enforce_on_create`, and a list of `{context, integration_id?}`.\n- **RepositoryRole IDs:** GitHub's docs don't list them. The Terraform provider docs give \"maintain -> 2, write -> 4, admin -> 5\" (https://github.com/integrations/terraform-provider-github/blob/main/docs/resources/repository_ruleset.md).\n\n**A2. Can GitHub Actions or `GITHUB_TOKEN` bypass a ruleset? No.**\n- Docs (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/creating-rulesets-for-a-repository) list the eligible actors as: \"Repository admins…; The maintain or write role…; Teams…; GitHub Apps; Dependabot.\" The GitHub Actions app is not selectable.\n- The request to allow it has been open since 2022 (https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/13836).\n- A GitHub staff reply explains why: the Actions identity isn't tied to one branch, so a bypass would let any branch's workflow skip protections (https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/25305).\n- Recursion rule: \"events triggered by the GITHUB_TOKEN will not create a new workflow run\" (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow).\n- **Alternatives, in order of preference:**\n  1. Release through a PR, so no bypass is needed.\n  2. A personal GitHub App. Generate a token with `actions/create-github-app-token`, and add the App as bypass actor `Integration` with `actor_id` set to the App ID. Use `persist-credentials: false` in checkout; otherwise pushes still go out with `GITHUB_TOKEN` and are blocked (discussions /136531, /110674).\n  3. A write deploy key with bypass actor `DeployKey`, `actor_id` null. It supports `always` mode only.\n\n**A3. Skipped checks** (https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/collaborating-on-repositories-with-code-quality-features/troubleshooting-required-status-checks)\n- \"A workflow is skipped by path filtering, branch filtering, or a commit message | Associated checks stay in a \"Pending\" state and block merging | Avoid requiring workflows that can be skipped.\"\n- \"A job is skipped by a conditional | The job reports \"Success\"\"\n- \"A job depends on a failed job | The dependent job is skipped and may not block merging | Use always() with needs\"\n- The conditions page says the same: \"A job that is skipped will report its status as \"Success\". It will not prevent a pull request from merging, even if it is a required check.\" (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-jobs-with-conditions)\n- **Policy:** don't use `paths:` filters on required workflows. Do the path detection inside the workflow and gate jobs with `if:`. Add an aggregate gate job that uses `if: always()` and fails when any `needs` result is failure or cancelled.\n\n**A4. Free plan and self-approval**\n- \"Rulesets are available in public repositories with GitHub Free…\" (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets)\n- \"Pull request authors cannot approve their own pull requests.\" (https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/approving-a-pull-request-with-required-reviews)\n- With 0 required approvals: \"The pull request doesn't necessarily have to be approved, but it must be opened.\" (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets)\n- **Consequence:** a sole maintainer should set `required_approving_review_count: 0`, or add the admin role as a bypass actor with mode `pull_request`.\n\n## B. Dependency pinning\n\n**Dependabot** (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/ecosystems-supported-by-dependabot/supported-ecosystems-and-repositories)\n- \"Dependabot updates the version documentation of GitHub Actions when the comment is on the same line, such as actions/checkout@<commit> #<tag or link>\"\n- \"If the commit you use is not associated with any tag, Dependabot will update the GitHub Actions to the latest commit.\"\n- A `pre-commit` ecosystem now exists.\n\n**dependabot.yml keys** (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference)\n- Ecosystems: `github-actions` and `pip`. `pip` also covers pip-compile, pipenv and poetry; `uv` is a separate ecosystem.\n- `directories` \"supports globbing and the wildcard character *. These features are not supported by the directory key.\"\n- `groups` supports `patterns`, `exclude-patterns`, `dependency-type`, `update-types` and `group-by: dependency-name`.\n- `cooldown` keys are `default-days`, `semver-major/minor/patch-days`, and `include`/`exclude`. It is \"only available for version updates, not security updates.\"\n- Dependabot applies \"a default cooldown period of 3 days to version updates, even when cooldown is not configured.\"\n- Both `github-actions` and `pip` support `default-days`.\n\n**Other pinning tools**\n- **Renovate `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests`:** \"Pin `github-action` digests.\" It sets `{matchDepTypes:['action','workflow'], pinDigests:true}`. A variant, `pinGitHubActionDigestsToSemver`, also exists (https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/main/lib/config/presets/internal/helpers.preset.ts).\n- **pinact:** \"pinact is a CLI to pin GitHub Actions and Reusable Workflows. pinact can also update their versions and verify version comments.\" Active, last push 2026-10-15 (https://github.com/suzuki-shunsuke/pinact).\n- **ratchet:** \"automating the process of pinning and unpinning upstream versions\". It covers several CI systems. Active, last push 2026-07-18 (https://github.com/sethvargo/ratchet).\n\n## C. REST schema** (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules)\n- **Bypass actor types:** `Integration`, `OrganizationAdmin`, `RepositoryRole`, `Team`, `DeployKey`, `User`.\n- **Bypass modes:** `always` (the default), `pull_request`, `exempt`.\n  - \"OrganizationAdmin is not applicable for personal repositories.\"\n  - \"If actor_type is DeployKey, this should be null.\"\n  - \"pull_request is only applicable to branch rulesets. When bypass_mode is exempt, rules will not be run for that actor and a bypass audit entry will not be created.\" Exempt mode was added on 2025-09-10 (https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-10-github-ruleset-exemptions-and-repository-insights-updates/).\n- **Branch conditions:** `include` \"Also accepts ~DEFAULT_BRANCH … or ~ALL\". `enforcement` is disabled, active or evaluate; evaluate is Enterprise only.\n- **Rules with no parameters:** `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`, `required_linear_history`.\n- **`pull_request` parameters:** `required_approving_review_count`, `dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push`, `require_code_owner_review`, `require_last_push_approval`, `required_review_thread_resolution`, `allowed_merge_methods` (merge, squash, rebase).\n- **`required_status_checks` parameters:** `strict_required_status_checks_policy` (\"must be tested with the latest code\"), `do_not_enforce_on_create`, and a list of `{context, integration_id?}`.\n- **RepositoryRole IDs:** GitHub's docs don't list them. The Terraform provider docs give \"maintain -> 2, write -> 4, admin -> 5\" (https://github.com/integrations/terraform-provider-github/blob/main/docs/resources/repository_ruleset.md).\n\n**A2. Can GitHub Actions or `GITHUB_TOKEN` bypass a ruleset? No.**\n- Docs (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/creating-rulesets-for-a-repository) list the eligible actors as: \"Repository admins…; The maintain or write role…; Teams…; GitHub Apps; Dependabot.\" The GitHub Actions app is not selectable.\n- The request to allow it has been open since 2022 (https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/13836).\n- A GitHub staff reply explains why: the Actions identity isn't tied to one branch, so a bypass would let any branch's workflow skip protections (https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/25305).\n- Recursion rule: \"events triggered by the GITHUB_TOKEN will not create a new workflow run\" (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow).\n- **Alternatives, in order of preference:**\n  1. Release through a PR, so no bypass is needed.\n  2. A personal GitHub App. Generate a token with `actions/create-github-app-token`, and add the App as bypass actor `Integration` with `actor_id` set to the App ID. Use `persist-credentials: false` in checkout; otherwise pushes still go out with `GITHUB_TOKEN` and are blocked (discussions /136531, /110674).\n  3. A write deploy key with bypass actor `DeployKey`, `actor_id` null. It supports `always` mode only.\n\n**A3. Skipped checks** (https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/collaborating-on-repositories-with-code-quality-features/troubleshooting-required-status-checks)\n- \"A workflow is skipped by path filtering, branch filtering, or a commit message | Associated checks stay in a \"Pending\" state and block merging | Avoid requiring workflows that can be skipped.\"\n- \"A job is skipped by a conditional | The job reports \"Success\"\"\n- \"A job depends on a failed job | The dependent job is skipped and may not block merging | Use always() with needs\"\n- The conditions page says the same: \"A job that is skipped will report its status as \"Success\". It will not prevent a pull request from merging, even if it is a required check.\" (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-jobs-with-conditions)\n- **Policy:** don't use `paths:` filters on required workflows. Do the path detection inside the workflow and gate jobs with `if:`. Add an aggregate gate job that uses `if: always()` and fails when any `needs` result is failure or cancelled.\n\n**A4. Free plan and self-approval**\n- \"Rulesets are available in public repositories with GitHub Free…\" (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets)\n- \"Pull request authors cannot approve their own pull requests.\" (https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/approving-a-pull-request-with-required-reviews)\n- With 0 required approvals: \"The pull request doesn't necessarily have to be approved, but it must be opened.\" (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets)\n- **Consequence:** a sole maintainer should set `required_approving_review_count: 0`, or add the admin role as a bypass actor with mode `pull_request`.\n\n## B. A real run on a GitHub-hosted CPU runner\n\nThe `cpu-smoke` job of the Model Tests workflow ran twice on pull request\ncommits, with the same model, script and inputs:\n[run 38550186566](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/actions/runs/38550186566) (run A) and [run 38552481450](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/actions/runs/38552481450) (run B). The script leaves\none of the 4 vCPUs free, so it used 3 threads.\n\n### Speed\n\nFrom `llama-timings.txt` of each run. \"Text\" is the 2 diagnosis requests\nplus the text request of `tests/test_real_models.py`. \"Image\" is the 2 X-ray\nand 2 prescription requests plus the image request of the same test file.\n\n| Request | Prompt tokens | Prompt time, run A | Prompt time, run B | Answer speed, run A | Answer speed, run B |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| Text (3 requests) | 66–68 | 2.0–2.2 s (**30–33 tokens/s**) | 2.5–2.6 s (25–27 tokens/s) | 7.9–8.0 tokens/s | 11.6 tokens/s |\n| One image (5 requests) | 288–307 | 65.8–66.7 s (**4.4–4.6 tokens/s**) | 83.6–84.5 s (3.4–3.6 tokens/s) | 7.6–7.8 tokens/s | 10.8–11.3 tokens/s |\n| Whole `Run medbench` step | | 377 s | 458 s | | |\n\n* **Writing the answer: 7.6–11.6 tokens/s**, two to three times the dev VM\n  (4.2 with 4 threads). The calculator used to say 4.3 for the runner; it\n  is now tuned to run A.\n* **Reading an image costs about 56–74 s.** A text prompt of 300 tokens\n  would take about 10–12 s. The rest is the image encoder (SigLIP,\n  896 × 896 pixels), which llama.cpp runs much less efficiently on CPU than\n  the text model. On CPU, image tasks are slow because of image reading, not\n  answer writing.\n* **Hosted runners are not all the same machine.** Run B wrote answers 45%\n  faster but read images 27% slower than run A. GitHub does not say which\n  CPU a runner gets, so timing tests in CI need a wide margin, and speed\n  comparisons between models must run on the same machine.\n\n### Scores\n\nThese runs used the inputs of the first version, which were generated by\ncode: a toy diagnosis table, prescriptions rendered in a handwriting-style\nfont and drawn X-ray phantoms. They were later replaced by real, openly\nlicensed files ([data-sources.md](data-sources.md)). 2 items per task, so\nthe scores show that the pipeline works, not how good the model is:\n\n| Task | Run A | Run B | Mean time per item, A / B |\n| --- | --- | --- | ---: |\n| diagnosis | top-1 1.0, top-5 1.0, MRR 1.0 | same | 6.5 s / 5.7 s |\n| ocr-prescription | CER 0.010, WER 0.056, drug + strength recall 1.0 | CER 0.051, WER 0.222, drug + strength recall 0.67 | 73.0 s / 88.8 s |\n| imaging-xray | sensitivity 0.0, specificity 0.0, accuracy 0.0 | same | 67.9 s / 85.4 s |\n\n**The same model gave a different answer to the same image.** For the\nsecond prescription, run A read \"levothyroxine 25 mcg tablet TiD x 3 days\"\nand run B read \"I evothyr oxin n° 25 mfg tablet TiDx 3 days\". Decoding is\ngreedy in both runs, so the reason is the CPU: different machines add\nfloating-point numbers in a different order, a near tie between two tokens\nflips, and the rest of the answer follows the new token. So OCR scores need\nmany items and confidence intervals, and a regression test must not expect\none exact string from a real model. A third run\n([38553921579](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/actions/runs/38553921579),\n353 s for the medbench step) gave run A's answers again: CER 0.0102,\ndiagnosis 2/2 and X-ray 0/2.\n\nThe X-ray result was checked by hand with the first version of\n[`experiments/issue1_xray_truth.py`](../../../experiments/issue1_xray_truth.py)\n(it now prints the labels of the real images), and both runs gave the same\nanswers:\n\n| Item | Truth | Model answer | Verdict |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| xray-00000 | nodule in the patient's right lung | \"No\" | missed finding |\n| xray-00001 | no finding | \"Yes, there is a round lung nodule in the patient's right lung.\" | false alarm |\n\nThe answers were read correctly; the model was wrong on both images. The\nphantom was a few ellipses, not a real X-ray, so this does not say how\nMedGemma reads real chest films. This is one reason the drawn images were\nreplaced by real, openly licensed X-rays ([data-sources.md](data-sources.md)).\nIt does show why one score from 2 items means nothing, and why Phase 2 of the [research plan](research-plan.md) uses\npublic X-rays with many items and confidence intervals.\n\nThe two real-model tests in `tests/` (one text request and one image\nrequest) passed in 76 s (run A) and 92 s (run B). [2026-10-16T16:50:38.765Z] [INFO]           "content": "# Evaluation validity: what a medbench score can show\n\nThis page lists what we checked about the benchmark's labels, splits,\nsample sizes, scoring rules and sources. It also lists what we could not\ncheck. It answers [issue #7](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/issues/7).\n\nThe short version: the real teaching images and pages are a **smoke test**.\nThey show that a model can read real files and answer in a usable format.\nThey are far too few, and too easy, to rank models or support a clinical\nclaim. The labels were reviewed by the maintainers, **not by clinicians**.\n\n## Label review\n\n`src/medbench/data/label_review.json` has one entry for each of the 37 real\nimages and pages. You can print it with:\n\n```bash\nmedbench review                     # every task\nmedbench review --task imaging-xray # one task\n```\n\nEach entry records:\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `view` | Projection, sequence or plane, as stated by the source. Two X-rays are **AP**, not PA: on AP, heart and mediastinum look larger. The X-ray prompt no longer says every X-ray is frontal PA. |\n| `laterality` | The side of the finding and how it was read. Sides are the **patient's** side. On X-ray and MRI that is mirrored in the image (radiological convention). Ultrasound sides that the source does not state are not scored. |\n| `label_source` | Where the label comes from: the Commons uploader's description, the RxHandBD dataset's own label, or a proofread Wikisource transcription. |\n| `source_group` | Items that may share a patient, uploader or source. Splits keep a group together. |\n| `uncertainty` | Known doubts, e.g. \"projection not stated\", \"side cannot be checked from pixels\", \"only *mass* is scorable, not the histology\". |\n| `also_present` | Other true findings that a good answer may name (e.g. mediastinal shift with a large effusion). |\n\nHow the review was done (`method` in the file): each label was read from the\nsource page and compared with the image or scan by eye; doubts were written\ndown. Nobody with medical training checked the images. `clinician_reviewed`\nis `false` and stays `false` until a clinician signs the file. A test\n(`tests/test_medbench_validity.py`) checks that the review covers exactly the\nreal imaging and OCR samples and that its sides match the scored `side`.\n\n### Class balance and source overlap\n\n| Task | Normal | Abnormal |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| `imaging-xray` | 3 | 6 |\n| `imaging-mri` | 3 | 4 |\n| `imaging-ultrasound` | 3 | 7 |\n\nAll three tasks have more abnormal than normal items. A model that always\nanswers \"abnormal\" gets 67–70% accuracy, so read sensitivity and\nspecificity, not accuracy.\n\nThe items are not independent. Hellerhoff uploaded 8 of the 26 images\n(X-ray, MRI and ultrasound). Häggström, Heilman, Novak and the\n`ptrump16` account uploaded 2–4 each. Images from one uploader share\nequipment, style and post-processing. `medbench.validity.LabelReview.group_of`\nreturns that group, so a split never puts one uploader's images on both\nsides.\n\n## Splits\n\n`medbench.validity.split_of` gives each group a fixed split (60% train,\n20% dev, 20% test) from a SHA-256 hash of `medbench-split-v1:<group>`. The\nsame group always lands in the same split. Adding data does not move old\nitems. `grouped_split` applies it to a list and never splits a group.\n\n* **DDXPlus.** Each row is a separate synthetic patient, so the row id is\n  the group. `medbench run --task diagnosis-ddxplus --split dev` takes dev\n  patients only. Tune prompts and parsers on `dev` and report on `test`. If\n  you leave out `--split`, the task keeps the old behaviour: the first rows\n  of the test file, so the numbers compare with older reports.\n* **Teaching images and pages.** With 14 source groups, a 60/20/20 split\n  gives 30 train, 6 dev and 1 test item. That is not a usable split. These\n  37 items are **test-only**: do not tune prompts, parsers or thresholds on\n  them, and `--split` does not apply to them. The prompts and parsers were\n  written before these items were scored, and no parameter was fitted to\n  them. Any later change that is checked against them must be reported as\n  such.\n\n## Sample-size targets\n\n`medbench.validity.required_sample_size` finds the smallest test set whose\n95% Wilson interval is at most ± a chosen half-width. `medbench review`\nprints the targets:\n\n| Task | Metric | Expected | ± | Needed | Have now |\n|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| `diagnosis-ddxplus` | top-1 accuracy | 0.5 | 0.05 | 381 patients | up to 134,529 in the test file |\n| imaging (per finding) | sensitivity and specificity | 0.8 | 0.10 | 60 per class | 3–7 per class |\n| OCR | key-term recall | 0.8 | 0.05 | 245 key terms | about 60 |\n\nThe half-widths are planning choices, not clinical standards. For ±3 points\nat 50%, 1,064 items are needed. Imaging needs real public sets (e.g.\nNIH ChestX-ray14, VinDr-CXR, BUSI) with their own licenses and splits; see\n[data-sources.md](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/data-sources.md).\n\n## Metrics and answer quality\n\nEvery report has:\n\n* `requested_items`, `items_run` and `coverage` (`items_run / items_requested`),\n  so a run that stops at its time budget is visible.\n* A Wilson 95% interval for each proportion (`metrics.wilson_interval`).\n  Unlike the bootstrap, it does not shrink to a point when 2 of 2 answers\n  are right: (0.34, 1.0).\n* `invalid_rate` (the parser found no answer), `abstention_rate` (the\n  answer declines or says it is unsure), `empty_rate` and `truncation_rate`\n  (the answer used all of `max_tokens`).\n\n### Ranked diagnosis parser\n\n`parse_ranked_diagnoses` matches the 49 DDXPlus condition names and their\naliases as whole words only. It skips lines that rule a diagnosis out. Tests\n(`tests/test_medbench_ddxplus_parser.py`) cover:\n\n* each of the 49 names and every alias;\n* adversarial outputs that the old substring match got wrong: \"measles\"\n  read as SLE, \"parainfluenza\" as influenza, and \"Not pneumonia\" as\n  pneumonia;\n* a network test that checks the name list against the pinned\n  `release_conditions.json`.\n\n`experiments/issue11_ddxplus_parser_probe.py` shows the old and the new\nparser side by side.\n\n### Negation, doses and OCR\n\n`medbench.clinical_text` replaces plain keyword overlap with explicit rules:\n\n* `affirmed_mention` is a NegEx-style check (Chapman et al., 2001). \"No\n  pneumothorax\" no longer earns credit for finding a pneumothorax. It also\n  handles pseudo-negations (\"cannot be ruled out\") and clause breaks\n  (\"but\").\n* `extract_doses` and `compare_doses` read number and unit pairs with\n  canonical units, so \"5 mg\" vs \"5 mcg\" counts as a unit error and \"50 mg\"\n  vs \"500 mg\" as a value error.\n* `normalise_ocr` applies Unicode NFKC, case folding and number/unit spacing\n  before CER and WER. Raw CER is still reported.\n* Imaging side accuracy uses the patient-side convention above.\n\nThese rules were checked on hand-written examples in\n`tests/test_medbench_clinical_text.py`. Those examples are **not\nexpert-reviewed**. Known gaps: uncertainty words (\"possible\", \"likely\") are\nnot graded, finding synonyms are a short fixed list, and there is no\nfinding-level localisation beyond left/right/both. An expert-reviewed\nexample set is still open (see \"What is still open\").\n\n## Source terms and provenance\n\n* Original code stays under the Unlicense. Data and model terms are kept\n  separately in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).\n* **Not every source is public domain.** The 37 teaching items are under\n  CC BY 4.0 (12), CC BY-SA 4.0 (9), CC BY-SA 3.0 (6), CC0 (5), public domain\n  (5), CC BY 3.0 (2) and CC BY 2.5 (1). DDXPlus and RxHandBD are CC BY 4.0.\n* Labels come from the uploaders' descriptions and the dataset authors.\n  Short quotes and the derived labels in `real_samples.json` and\n  `label_review.json` keep their source's attribution. Images and crops\n  derived from CC BY-SA files keep the share-alike license. `medbench fetch`\n  writes `ATTRIBUTION.md`, and each report lists its `sources`.\n* The five history pages are public domain in the US. Fothergill died in\n  1955, so his 1907 book became public domain in \"life + 70\" countries only\n  on 1 January 2026. Check your own jurisdiction before you redistribute\n  the scans.\n\n## Baselines and ready evaluation libraries\n\n| Tool | License (checked on GitHub) | Use here |\n|---|---|---|\n| [Tesseract](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tesseract) | Apache-2.0 | `--backend tesseract`; the `ocr-baseline` CI job runs it on both OCR tasks and uploads JSON reports. |\n| [PaddleOCR](https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR) | Apache-2.0 | Next OCR baseline; needs a GPU or a slow CPU run. |\n| [TorchXRayVision](https://github.com/mlmed/torchxrayvision) | Apache-2.0 (code; check each model's license) | Specialist chest X-ray classifier baseline for `imaging-xray`. |\n| [MedEvalKit](https://github.com/alibaba-damo-academy/MedEvalKit) | No LICENSE file (README badge says Apache-2.0) | Reference for medical VQA sets; do not vendor it until the license is clear. |\n| [VLMEvalKit](https://github.com/open-compass/VLMEvalKit) | Apache-2.0 | Wide VLM benchmark runner; useful for public medical VQA sets. |\n| [lmms-eval](https://github.com/EvolvingLMMs-Lab/lmms-eval) | MIT | Same, built on lm-evaluation-harness. |\n| [MultiMedEval](https://github.com/corentin-ryr/MultiMedEval) | MIT | Medical VLM suite (VQA, report generation, classification). |\n| [HealthBench (simple-evals)](https://github.com/openai/simple-evals) | MIT | Rubric-graded health conversations; text only. |\n| [medspaCy](https://github.com/medspacy/medspacy) / [negspaCy](https://github.com/jenojp/negspacy) | MIT | Fuller ConText/NegEx; our rules are a small dependency-free subset. |\n| [Hugging Face evaluate](https://github.com/huggingface/evaluate) | Apache-2.0 | Standard CER/WER for cross-checking our edit distance. |\n\nmedbench does not replace these tools. It runs a small set of real,\nlicense-checked files on the hardware we have, with the same answer-quality\ncounters for every backend. The library runs and the specialist baselines\nare the next step in [research-plan.md](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/research-plan.md).\n\nReproducible reports: the `ocr-baseline` job in\n`.github/workflows/model-tests.yml` installs Ubuntu's `tesseract-ocr` and\nruns every OCR item. It uploads the reports and `tesseract-version.txt` as\nthe `medbench-ocr-baseline-reports` artifact. Model reports from the GPU\nrunner are uploaded the same way.\n\n## What is still open\n\n* A clinician has not reviewed the labels or the scoring examples.\n  `clinician_reviewed` must stay `false` until one does.\n* The teaching set is far below the sample-size targets. Public sets with\n  patient-level splits are needed before any model comparison.\n* PaddleOCR, TorchXRayVision and the evaluation libraries above have not\n  been run in this repository yet.\n"
