[2026-10-16T16:50:38.820Z] [INFO]     "content": "# Evaluation validity: what a medbench score can show\n\nThis page lists what we checked about the benchmark's labels, splits,\nsample sizes, scoring rules and sources. It also lists what we could not\ncheck. It answers [issue #7](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/issues/7).\n\nThe short version: the real teaching images and pages are a **smoke test**.\nThey show that a model can read real files and answer in a usable format.\nThey are far too few, and too easy, to rank models or support a clinical\nclaim. The labels were reviewed by the maintainers, **not by clinicians**.\n\n## Label review\n\n`src/medbench/data/label_review.json` has one entry for each of the 37 real\nimages and pages. You can print it with:\n\n```bash\nmedbench review                     # every task\nmedbench review --task imaging-xray # one task\n```\n\nEach entry records:\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `view` | Projection, sequence or plane, as stated by the source. Two X-rays are **AP**, not PA: on AP, heart and mediastinum look larger. The X-ray prompt no longer says every X-ray is frontal PA. |\n| `laterality` | The side of the finding and how it was read. Sides are the **patient's** side. On X-ray and MRI that is mirrored in the image (radiological convention). Ultrasound sides that the source does not state are not scored. |\n| `label_source` | Where the label comes from: the Commons uploader's description, the RxHandBD dataset's own label, or a proofread Wikisource transcription. |\n| `source_group` | Items that may share a patient, uploader or source. Splits keep a group together. |\n| `uncertainty` | Known doubts, e.g. \"projection not stated\", \"side cannot be checked from pixels\", \"only *mass* is scorable, not the histology\". |\n| `also_present` | Other true findings that a good answer may name (e.g. mediastinal shift with a large effusion). |\n\nHow the review was done (`method` in the file): each label was read from the\nsource page and compared with the image or scan by eye; doubts were written\ndown. Nobody with medical training checked the images. `clinician_reviewed`\nis `false` and stays `false` until a clinician signs the file. A test\n(`tests/test_medbench_validity.py`) checks that the review covers exactly the\nreal imaging and OCR samples and that its sides match the scored `side`.\n\n### Class balance and source overlap\n\n| Task | Normal | Abnormal |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| `imaging-xray` | 3 | 6 |\n| `imaging-mri` | 3 | 4 |\n| `imaging-ultrasound` | 3 | 7 |\n\nAll three tasks have more abnormal than normal items. A model that always\nanswers \"abnormal\" gets 67–70% accuracy, so read sensitivity and\nspecificity, not accuracy.\n\nThe items are not independent. Hellerhoff uploaded 8 of the 26 images\n(X-ray, MRI and ultrasound). Häggström, Heilman, Novak and the\n`ptrump16` account uploaded 2–4 each. Images from one uploader share\nequipment, style and post-processing. `medbench.validity.LabelReview.group_of`\nreturns that group, so a split never puts one uploader's images on both\nsides.\n\n## Splits\n\n`medbench.validity.split_of` gives each group a fixed split (60% train,\n20% dev, 20% test) from a SHA-256 hash of `medbench-split-v1:<group>`. The\nsame group always lands in the same split. Adding data does not move old\nitems. `grouped_split` applies it to a list and never splits a group.\n\n* **DDXPlus.** Each row is a separate synthetic patient, so the row id is\n  the group. `medbench run --task diagnosis-ddxplus --split dev` takes dev\n  patients only. Tune prompts and parsers on `dev` and report on `test`. If\n  you leave out `--split`, the task keeps the old behaviour: the first rows\n  of the test file, so the numbers compare with older reports.\n* **Teaching images and pages.** With 14 source groups, a 60/20/20 split\n  gives 30 train, 6 dev and 1 test item. That is not a usable split. These\n  37 items are **test-only**: do not tune prompts, parsers or thresholds on\n  them, and `--split` does not apply to them. The prompts and parsers were\n  written before these items were scored, and no parameter was fitted to\n  them. Any later change that is checked against them must be reported as\n  such.\n\n## Sample-size targets\n\n`medbench.validity.required_sample_size` finds the smallest test set whose\n95% Wilson interval is at most ± a chosen half-width. `medbench review`\nprints the targets:\n\n| Task | Metric | Expected | ± | Needed | Have now |\n|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| `diagnosis-ddxplus` | top-1 accuracy | 0.5 | 0.05 | 381 patients | up to 134,529 in the test file |\n| imaging (per finding) | sensitivity and specificity | 0.8 | 0.10 | 60 per class | 3–7 per class |\n| OCR | key-term recall | 0.8 | 0.05 | 245 key terms | about 60 |\n\nThe half-widths are planning choices, not clinical standards. For ±3 points\nat 50%, 1,064 items are needed. Imaging needs real public sets (e.g.\nNIH ChestX-ray14, VinDr-CXR, BUSI) with their own licenses and splits; see\n[data-sources.md](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1/data-sources.md).\n\n## Metrics and answer quality\n\nEvery report has:\n\n* `requested_items`, `items_run` and `coverage` (`items_run / items_requested`),\n  so a run that stops at its time budget is visible.\n* A Wilson 95% interval for each proportion (`metrics.wilson_interval`).\n  Unlike the bootstrap, it does not shrink to a point when 2 of 2 answers\n  are right: (0.34, 1.0).\n* `invalid_rate` (the parser found no answer), `abstention_rate` (the\n  answer declines or says it is unsure), `empty_rate` and `truncation_rate`\n  (the answer used all of `max_tokens`).\n\n### Ranked diagnosis parser\n\n`parse_ranked_diagnoses` matches the 49 DDXPlus condition names and their\naliases as whole words only. It skips lines that rule a diagnosis out. Tests\n(`tests/test_medbench_ddxplus_parser.py`) cover:\n\n* each of the 49 names and every alias;\n* adversarial outputs that the old substring match got wrong: \"measles\"\n  read as SLE, \"parainfluenza\" as influenza, and \"Not pneumonia\" as\n  pneumonia;\n* a network test that checks the name list against the pinned\n  `release_conditions.json`.\n\n`experiments/issue11_ddxplus_parser_probe.py` shows the old and the new\nparser side by side.\n\n### Negation, doses and OCR\n\n`medbench.clinical_text` replaces plain keyword overlap with explicit rules:\n\n* `affirmed_mention` is a NegEx-style check (Chapman et al., 2001). \"No\n  pneumothorax\" no longer earns credit for finding a pneumothorax. It also\n  handles pseudo-negations (\"cannot be ruled out\") and clause breaks\n  (\"but\").\n* `extract_doses` and `compare_doses` read number and unit pairs with\n  canonical units, so \"5 mg\" vs \"5 mcg\" counts as a unit error and \"50 mg\"\n  vs \"500 mg\" as a value error.\n* `normalise_ocr` applies Unicode NFKC, case folding and number/unit spacing\n  before CER and WER. Raw CER is still reported.\n* Imaging side accuracy uses the patient-side convention above.\n\nThese rules were checked on hand-written examples in\n`tests/test_medbench_clinical_text.py`. Those examples are **not\nexpert-reviewed**. Known gaps: uncertainty words (\"possible\", \"likely\") are\nnot graded, finding synonyms are a short fixed list, and there is no\nfinding-level localisation beyond left/right/both. An expert-reviewed\nexample set is still open (see \"What is still open\").\n\n## Source terms and provenance\n\n* Original code stays under the Unlicense. Copying\n# the weights into RAM avoids that, but only when they fit with room to spare.\nchoose_load_mode() {\n  if [[ \"$LOAD_MODE\" != auto ]]; then\n    echo \"$LOAD_MODE\"\n    return\n  fi\n  if ((GPU_LAYERS > 0)); UniMedVL: it has no GGUF build, so run it with PyTorch on a 40 GB+ GPU\n   through `TransformersBackend` or a vLLM/SGLang server, and point\n   `medbench run --backend openai --base-url ...` at it.\n\nResources from `medbench estimate` (raw output in\n[data/estimates.txt](data/estimates.txt)). 120 requests = 6 tasks × 20 items, an upper bound for today's\nabout 77 requests:\n\n| Model | Where | Memory | Speed | 120 requests (full set) |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| MedGemma 4B Q4 | GitHub CPU runner | 3.8 GB | 7.8–11.6 tokens/s measured; 66–84 s to read each image | about 2–2.5 hours |\n| MedGemma 4B Q4 | L4 24 GB | 3.8 GB | 65 tokens/s | about 8 minutes |\n| MedGemma 27B Q4 | L4 24 GB | 18.3 GB | 10 tokens/s | about 51 minutes |\n| MedGemma 27B bf16 | A100 80 GB | 56.3 GB | 22 tokens/s | about 24 minutes |\n| UniMedVL bf16 | A100 80 GB | 30.2 GB | 80 tokens/s | about 7 minutes |\n\nAlternatives for running models:\n\n| Option | Pros | Cons |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| **llama.cpp `llama-server` (chosen)** | One binary, CPU and GPU, 4-bit GGUF, vision support, pinned by SHA-256 | Only models with GGUF conversions (no UniMedVL) |\n| Ollama | Easiest install | Hides versions and files; harder to pin |\n| vLLM / SGLang | Fastest on GPU, many users at once | GPU only, large install |\n| Hugging Face Transformers | Every model, including UniMedVL | Slow on CPU, needs a large PyTorch install |\n| Cloud APIs | No hardware | Not allowed for credentialed data, costs per call, results change over time |\n\n**Done when:** both MedGemma sizes have a JSON report for every task, and\nthe speed numbers are added to [measurements.md](measurements.md).\n\n----\n    M --> M1[MedGemma 1.5 4B or Hulu-Med for 3D<br/>+ nnU-Net / TotalSegmentator for measurements]\n    U --> U1[Task network fine-tuned on HC18 / BUSI<br/>check each license<br/>VLMs are weak here]\n```\n\nThe real-model tests in this repository start with **MedGemma 4B** (fits\nin CPU CI) and **MedGemma 27B** (GPU runner), because the issue names\nMedGemma, and llama.cpp can run both from the same script. The rulesets are files in\n`.github/rulesets/`; `tests/test_repository_policy.py` keeps this page, the\nfiles and the workflows consistent.\n\n**Status (2026-10-16): written, not applied.** The live repository has no\nruleset and no branch protection. Rules that block pushes change how the\nrelease writer works, so a repository admin applies them deliberately (see\n[Applying the Rulesets](#applying-the-rulesets)); until then the\n`Branch Rulesets` job fails on main with the command to run.\n\n## Required Checks\n\n`.github/rulesets/main-checks.json` requires three terminal status gates,\neach reported by GitHub Actions (integration 15368, so no other app or\ncommit status can satisfy them):\n\n| Check | Workflow | Covers |\n|---|---|---|\n| `Pipeline Status (CI/CD)` | `release.yml` | lint, format, secret scan, docs validation, Python 3.13 tests, build, changelog fragment, Docker build, release preflight (report mode) |\n| `Pipeline Status (Compatibility)` | `compatibility.yml` | Python 3.9 runtime on Linux, full suite on macOS arm64 |\n| `Pipeline Status (Security)` | `security.yml` | `pip-audit` of every dependency surface, CodeQL (Python and Actions), Dependency Review, Dependency graph, branch rulesets |\n\nA gate observes every other job of its workflow with `if: always()`, so a\njob that failed, timed out or was cancelled fails the gate (issue #69). Each\ngate has its own name: before issue #10 all seven were called\n`Pipeline Status`, and a required context with that name could be satisfied\nby whichever workflow happened to finish.\n\nOnly workflows that run on **every** pull request can be required: a\nworkflow skipped by a `paths` filter never reports, and GitHub waits for a\nmissing required check forever. `compatibility.yml` therefore no longer\nfilters pull requests. The path-filtered gates (`Docs`, `Links`,\n`Model Tests`, `Workflows`) still run when their files change and still turn\nmain red; they are not required.\n\n`strict_required_status_checks_policy` is off: `pull_request` runs already\ntest the merge with the current base, and requiring an up-to-date branch\nwould force a rebase of every open pull request (Dependabot's included)\nafter each merge. The gates on main catch what a stale merge breaks.\n\n## Pull Request Review\n\n`.github/rulesets/main-review.json` requires a pull request with one\napproval for every change to main. A new push dismisses the approval and\nevery review thread must be resolved.\n\nContributor pull requests need the maintainer's approval. The maintainer\ncannot approve their own pull request, so the `admin` repository role\n(`actor_id` 5) may bypass this ruleset **in pull-request mode only**: they\ncan merge their own pull request without a second reviewer, but cannot push\nto main directly. The required checks and the history rules are separate\nrulesets without this bypass, so an admin merge still waits for green gates.\n\n`.github/rulesets/main-history.json` forbids force pushes and deleting main\nfor everyone, with no bypass at all; the release writer only fast-forwards.\n\n## Release Bot Bypass\n\n`manual-release` in `release.yml` pushes the version commit to main with the\njob's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`scripts/version_and_commit.py`), as\n`github-actions[bot]`. A direct push has no pull request and no checks, so\nthe GitHub Actions app (`Integration`, `actor_id` 15368) bypasses\n`main-checks` and `main-review` in `always` mode, which keeps an audit entry\nfor every bypass (`exempt` would not). `auto-release` publishes the version\nthat a merged pull request already committed and pushes nothing.\n\nWhat keeps this bypass narrow:\n\n- Fork pull requests get a read-only token; no workflow uses\n  `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run`.\n- Only `auto-release` and `manual-release` request `contents: write`, and\n  they run only on a push to main or a manual dispatch, after lint, tests,\n  build and the credential preflight succeeded.\n- A collaborator could still write a workflow on their own branch that uses\n  the bypass. With one maintainer that is the same trust they already have;\n  before adding collaborators, replace the app bypass with a deploy key that\n  only a protected `release` environment can read (actor type `DeployKey`),\n  and change the `manual-release` checkout to use it.\n\nThe bypass actor id 15368 and role id 5 come from GitHub's REST schema and\nother public rulesets; GitHub does not document a table of them. The first\nmanual release after applying the rulesets is the test (see\n[Test Plan](#test-plan)).\n\n## Fork Pull Requests\n\nA `pull_request` run from a fork has a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`, no OIDC\ntoken and no secrets. Every secret a workflow reads, and why a fork run is\nstill safe:\n\n| Secret | Jobs | On a fork pull request |\n|---|---|---|\n| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | `links.yml` link-checker; `auto-release`, `manual-release` | read-only token; the release jobs do not run |\n| `CODECOV_TOKEN` | `test` | empty, so the upload step is skipped (`test_release_workflow_gates_codecov_upload_on_token`) |\n| `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME`, `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` | `release-preflight`, `docker-publish*` | preflight runs in `report` mode and only annotates; publishing jobs do not run |\n\nThe release preflight cannot exchange an OIDC token in a fork, and the\nDependency graph and branch ruleset checks are repository settings, so all\nthree report instead of failing a contributor's pull request; on main they\nfail.\n\n## Tokens and Credentials\n\n- Every workflow defaults to `contents: read`; write scopes are granted per\n  job. `tests/test_repository_policy.py` lists the ten write scopes that\n  exist today, so a new one fails the tests until this section is reviewed.\n- Every checkout sets `persist-credentials: false` except `manual-release`,\n  which needs the token in `.git/config` for its `git push origin main`.\n- `id-token: [REDACTED] is held by the release jobs and the preflight (PyPI\n  trusted publishing) and by the Pages deploy.\n\n## Action Pins and Update Pull Requests\n\nEvery `uses:` names a full commit hash with the release in a comment\n(`actions/checkout@3d3c42e… # v7.0.1`); zizmor's `hash-pin` policy enforces\nit, and its `ref-version-mismatch` audit checks that the comment matches the\nhash. `.github/dependabot.yml` opens weekly, grouped update pull requests\nfor actions and for the Python dependencies in `pyproject.toml` and\n`docs/requirements.txt`, after a seven-day cooldown. Those pull requests run\nthe same required checks and need the same review: read the release notes,\ncheck that the runner image and Python versions are still supported, and\nlet `pip-audit` and Dependency Review run.\n\n`scripts/unimedvl-requirements.txt` is not updated by Dependabot: its torch\npin has to match the hash-pinned flash-attn wheel. `pip-audit` still checks\nit on every run (`scripts/audit_dependencies.py`).\n\nGitHub can also reject any workflow that uses an action by tag\n(Settings → Actions → General → \"Require actions to be pinned to a full-length\ncommit SHA\", `sha_pinning_required`). It is off today; every action here is\nalready pinned, so a repository admin can turn it on at any time.\n\n## Self-Hosted Runners\n\nNo self-hosted runner is attached today (0 registered on 2026-10-16). The\n`gpu` job of `model-tests.yml` is the only job that may use one, and the\nfollowing holds before a GPU host is attached:\n\n- **Trusted dispatch only.** The job runs only for a manual\n  `workflow_dispatch` from main with `gpu: true`, never for a pull request,\n  a schedule or a dispatch from another branch (whose workflow file anyone\n  with push access could have changed). Only users with write access can\n  dispatch.\n- **Approval.** The job uses the `gpu` environment. Before attaching a\n  runner, open Settings → Environments → `gpu`, restrict deployment branches\n  to `main` and add the maintainer as a required reviewer.\n- **Least privilege.** `contents: read`, no secrets, no persisted\n  credentials; models and archives are pinned by revision and SHA-256.\n- **Ephemeral and isolated.** Register the runner with\n  `./config.sh --ephemeral` on a fresh VM or container per job (a cloud GPU\n  that is destroyed afterwards), in a repository-level runner group used by\n  this repository only, with the labels `self-hosted, linux, x64, gpu`. Do\n  not attach a personal workstation.\n- **Cleanup.** The run script stops the model server on exit or deadline\n  (`tests/test_medbench_model_run.py`), and the last step removes the\n  downloaded weights, the model virtual environment and the reports even\n  when the job failed. Reports are uploaded as artifacts first.\n\n## Trusted Publishing (#8) and Required Checks\n\nPyPI trusted publishing for `medical-neural-network-ml` is not configured\nyet (issue #8). The release preflight proves it with the real OIDC\nexchange, so:\n\n- On pull requests the preflight runs in `report` mode: it annotates the\n  missing publisher and passes. `Pipeline Status (CI/CD)` stays green and\n  contributors are not blocked by a setting they cannot change.\n- On main and on a manual release it runs in `release` mode and fails with\n  `release-preflight: refusing to release` and the PyPI settings to enter.\n  `auto-release` and `manual-release` do not run, so no version commit is\n  pushed and nothing is published.\n\nThat failure is intentional and must not be turned into a pass: no\n`continue-on-error`, no skipped preflight, no bypass for it. It turns green\nwhen a maintainer registers the publisher (owner `konard`, repository\n`medical-neural-network-ml`, workflow `release.yml`, environment blank).\n\n## Applying the Rulesets\n\nA repository admin, after reading this page:\n\n```bash\n# Read-only comparison with the live repository.\npython scripts/repository_rulesets.py check --repository konard/medical-neural-network-ml\n# Print the API calls (dry run, nothing changes).\nGH_TOKEN=[REDACTED] auth token) python scripts/repository_rulesets.py apply --repository konard/medical-neural-network-ml\n# Create or replace the three rulesets.\nGH_TOKEN=[REDACTED] auth token) python scripts/repository_rulesets.py apply --repository konard/medical-neural-network-ml --yes\n```\n\nA ruleset PUT replaces the whole ruleset, so change the JSON files, not the\nsettings page; the `Branch Rulesets` job of `security.yml` reports any\ndifference. To try the rules first, set `\"enforcement\": \"evaluate\"` in the\nfiles: GitHub then records what would have been blocked without blocking it.\n\n## Test Plan\n\nAfter applying the rulesets:\n\n1. **Contributor pull request.** From a fork, open a pull request that\n   changes a file under `src/`. The three gates must report, the merge must\n   wait for them and for one approval, and preflight, Dependency graph and\n   ruleset checks must only annotate.\n2. **Maintainer pull request.** The admin can merge their own green pull\n   request without an approval; a red one cannot be merged.\n3. **Direct push.** `git push origin main` from a maintainer clone is\n   rejected, as is `git push --force`.\n4. **Automatic version commit.** After #8, dispatch `CI/CD Pipeline` with a\n   `patch` bump. `manual-release` must push the version commit through the\n   GitHub Actions bypass (Settings → Rules → Insights shows the bypass). If\n   the push is rejected, replace the bypass with a deploy key as described\n   in [Release Bot Bypass](#release-bot-bypass); do not remove the rules.\n5. **Dependabot.** The first grouped update pull request runs the same\n   gates and needs the same approval.\n"

Fine-tuning memory and compute\n\n### 6.1 Memory per parameter\n\nHugging Face \"model memory anatomy\" for mixed-precision AdamW [S48]: weights 6 B/param (fp16 copy 2 + fp32 master 4), Adam states 8 B/param, gradients 4 B/param. That is **18 B/param plus activations**. A leaner bf16 setup (bf16 weights 2 + bf16 grads 2 + fp32 master/m/v 12) gives the often-quoted **~16 B/param**. 8-bit Adam reduces the optimiser states to 2 B/param.\n\n| Method | MedGemma 4B (4.3 B) | MedGemma 27B (27.4 B) | Notes |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Full FT, AdamW mixed precision (16-18 B/param) | ~69-77 GB + activations, so 1x H100 80GB is tight; plan for 2x | ~440-490 GB + activations, so **8x H100 80GB with FSDP/ZeRO-3** | estimate |\n| LoRA, 16-bit frozen base | ~9 GB base + adapters + activations, so ~12-20 GB | Unsloth minimum **64 GB** (27B row) [S49] | bf16 base needs no bf16-capable GPU for the weights, but compute benefits from bf16 |\n| QLoRA, 4-bit NF4 base (Dettmers et al. 2023) | ~3.5-6 GB (Unsloth: 3B → 3.5 GB, 7B → 5 GB) [S49] | Unsloth minimum **22 GB** [S49]; Unsloth Gemma 3 post: 27B \"fits in under 22GB\" [S9] | QLoRA paper: a 65B model on a single 48 GB GPU [S50] |\n\nSo QLoRA of MedGemma 27B fits on a 24 GB card (RTX 3090/4090, L4) at short sequence lengths and batch size 1-2. 32-48 GB (RTX 5090, A6000, L40S) leaves room for longer image+text sequences. QLoRA of 4B fits on a 16 GB T4 or an 8-12 GB consumer card. Unsloth requires CUDA compute capability ≥ 7.0, so T4 and V100 are supported [S49].\n\n### 6.2 Compute: FLOPs ≈ 6·N·D\n\n- Training compute is about 6 x N params x D tokens (forward 2N + backward 4N per token) [S51]. The Chinchilla compute-optimal data size is about **20 tokens per parameter** [S52].\n- H100 SXM bf16 dense: **989 TFLOPS** (NVIDIA lists 1,979 \"with sparsity\") [S39][S53]. Realistic MFU is **35-45%**. Llama 3 405B pre-training reported about 38-43% bf16 MFU on 8K-16K H100s, about 380-430 TFLOPS/GPU [S53]. Small single-node fine-tunes often reach only 20-40% **(unverified)**.\n\n# Hardware, CI/CD and resource research notes (issue #1)\n\nResearch date: 2026-10-14. A hosted Mac is not the same machine as this 18 GiB M3 Pro, and its\nlabel does not establish that Metal model inference is available.\n[GitHub runner specifications](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners).\n\n## Model inference\n\n| Model/path | Initial target | Evidence and limits |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| MedGemma 4B Q4_K_M, Linux CPU | 16 GB host, at least 6 GB free RAM, 8 GB free disk for setup and model | Existing measured CPU runs; 2.490 GB language file + 0.851 GB vision projector, then KV/cache/buffers |\n| Small SmolVLM, native MLX | M3 Pro with at least 2.4 GB reclaimable RAM for the conservative preflight; keep one image and short output | 145 MB checkpoint; text and one real X-ray request completed locally; medical answer formats failed |\n| MedGemma 4B, native MLX | 18 GiB Mac with sufficient free RAM; at least ~6.5 GB reclaimable for the 70% preflight, 8 GB model ceiling | 2.995 GB checkpoint + 1.5 GB minimum buffer allowance; not run on this busy Mac |\n| MedGemma 27B Q4_K_M, llama.cpp CUDA | NVIDIA 24 GB VRAM recommended, 32 GB+ host RAM, 50 GB free disk | 16.547 GB language file + 0.858 GB projector, plus cache/buffers. GPU workflow exists, measurements outstanding |\n| MedGemma 27B bf16 | 80 GB GPU is a conservative initial target | About 55 GB weights alone. A simple arithmetic fit on 64 GB does not prove runtime capacity |\n| UniMedVL bf16 | Dedicated CUDA host; start with 40 GB+ VRAM, 64 GB+ host RAM, 80 GB free disk | About 29.2 GB weights. `scripts/unimedvl_server.py` serves the pinned upstream code (commit `f51aa0a`) and weights (revision `29918ce`) in an isolated Python 3.10 environment; not yet run on a GPU. 40 GB is an unverified lower target; 80 GB provides more headroom |\n\nAll model runs must record context, image resolution, output length, batch,\nconcurrency and runtime version. Doubling these can change capacity. The\ncalculator includes pinned MedGemma projector bytes, but its generic overhead\nis still only a lower-order approximation. `fits` describes arithmetic\ncapacity, not runtime support. UniMedVL GGUF/NF4 combinations are theoretical\nuntil a compatible implementation is demonstrated.\n\nThe manual self-hosted job uses labels `[self-hosted, linux, x64, gpu]`,\nCUDA 12.8 llama.cpp binaries and a pinned runtime archive. No self-hosted\nrunner is registered in this repository yet. Check driver\ncompatibility with that CUDA release. A 16 GB T4 cannot hold the 27B Q4\nworking set. Never send public pull-request code directly to a persistent\nGPU runner. CPU smoke runs three tasks; the manual GPU job includes all\nseven, for `medgemma-4b-it`, `medgemma-27b-it` or `unimedvl`. Every download\nand run is wrapped in `medbench monitor`, which writes\n`medbench-reports/resources-*.json` (peak GPU and host memory, free disk,\ndriver and CUDA versions, wall time); the run also saves the server's cold\nstart time and metrics. Out-of-memory and timed-out items are recorded with\ntheir error and the run continues. The manual GPU task budget is 90 minutes, with a 95-minute outer deadline\nand a three-and-a-half-hour job limit for downloads, setup and artifact upload. This\nreplaces a 30-minute task budget that was shorter than the historical 27B\nestimate. Actual runtime still needs measurement; incomplete coverage fails\nexplicitly instead of silently passing.\n[Run and measure both large models](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/issues/6).\n\n## Fine-tuning and training\n\n`medbench estimate --finetune` estimates weights, trainable adapters,\noptimizer/gradients and activations. It does not allocate a real training\nstep, include every vision buffer, prove multi-GPU sharding, or implement a\ntraining workflow. The historical 4B/~4.9 GB and 27B/~19.6 GB QLoRA numbers\nare formula outputs, not safe minimum GPU recommendations. Start dedicated\nGPU profiling with batch 1 and explicit sequence/image limits before choosing\nhardware. Full Adam training stores several copies of model state; 27B can\nneed hundreds of GB distributed across GPUs, plus checkpoint storage.\n\nMLX LoRA and CUDA bitsandbytes NF4 are different implementations. Do not infer\nApple support from an NVIDIA QLoRA estimate. The estimator assumes linear\nspeedup across GPUs and fixed utilization, so its training duration/cost is\na planning calculation. It\nprints a low–high range (0.8–1.5 times the sum) for what the sum leaves out:\nallocator fragmentation, loading and dequantization buffers and vision\nactivations. It is a formula. These are its outputs for batch 1, LoRA rank 16\nand gradient checkpointing (raw output in\n`docs/case-studies/issue-1/data/finetune-estimates-20261016.txt`):\n\n| Model | Tokens | LoRA, bf16 base | QLoRA, NF4 base | Of which logits |\n| --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: |\n| MedGemma 4B | 512 / 2 048 | 12.9 / 19.9 GB (10–30) | 6.5 / 13.5 GB (5.2–20) | 2.1 / 8.6 GB |\n| UniMedVL | 512 / 2 048 | 32.7 / 37.1 GB (26–56) | 11.1 / 15.5 GB (8.8–23) | 1.2 / 5.0 GB |\n| MedGemma 27B | 512 / 2 048 | 60.8 / 68.9 GB (49–103) | 20.1 / 28.2 GB (16–42) | 2.1 / 8.6 GB |\n\nFull fine-tuning with AdamW is about 80 GB for 4B and 450 GB for 27B by the\nsame formula, so 27B needs several GPUs with sharded optimizer state. That\n27B QLoRA fits one 24 GB GPU is a hypothesis: it needs short sequences or a\nchunked/fused cross-entropy (Liger Kernel, Unsloth) that never holds the\nlogits of Gemma 3's 262 k-token vocabulary.\n\n`scripts/measure_training_memory.py` runs real optimizer steps with the\nsame inputs and writes one JSON report: the loading peak, the training peak\n(on CUDA also reserved minus allocated), gradient and optimizer-state bytes,\nthe image tokens the processor inserted, the size of a resumable checkpoint,\nlibrary versions, and measured/estimated ratios. Before loading, it compares\nthe high end of the estimate with free memory and refuses when less than\n10% would stay free. Out-of-memory, refusal and unsupported combinations\nstill write a report with their `status`.\n\n### Measured on a CPU, 2026-10-16\n\nNo GPU was available for this work, so the probe ran small models on a\n6-core x86 CPU in fp32, inside a 3.1 GB memory limit, with an outer watchdog\nthat kills a run above 2.3 GB. Reports and commands are in\n`docs/case-studies/issue-1/data/training-memory-cpu-20261016/`.\n\nTRAINING_TABLE\n\nWhat these show:\n\n- **The logits term is real.** From 256 to 1 024 tokens the SmolLM2 step peak\n  grew by 0.68 GB, about 18 bytes per token and vocabulary entry; the\n  estimator uses 16. With Gemma 3's vocabulary that is 8.6 GB at 2 048\n  tokens, more than the LoRA rank or the activations.\n- **The LoRA rank matters little.** Rank 8 to 64 added 0.23 GB on SmolLM2.\n- **Image tokens depend on processor settings, not only on image size.**\n  SmolVLM inserted 1 088 image tokens for one 512 px image with its default\n  image splitting and 64 with `--processor-arg do_image_splitting=false`.\n  Every report records the processor arguments and the measured count.\n- **Measured peaks are 0.6–0.9 of the estimate.** The estimate assumes bf16\n  weights plus 1.5 GB of GPU framework overhead (CUDA context, kernels);\n  these CPU runs held fp32 weights and had no CUDA context. They check how\n  the terms grow, not the absolute size of a GPU run.\n\n### Still to measure on dedicated GPUs\n\nMedGemma 4B and 27B need a CUDA host; QLoRA here means bitsandbytes NF4,\nwhich the probe runs only on CUDA:\n\n```bash\npython scripts/measure_training_memory.py --model google/medgemma-27b-it \\\\\n    --revision <commit> --method qlora --seq-len 512 --image-size 896 \\\\\n    --out medbench-reports/train-medgemma-27b-qlora-512.json\n```\n\nRepeat at `--seq-len 2048`, with `--method lora` on a card that fits it, and\nfor `google/medgemma-4b-it`. UniMedVL is not a transformers model, so the\nprobe cannot load it; its training needs the upstream code and has only the\nformula above. On the 18 GiB M3 Pro, only MedGemma 4B is worth trying, and\nonly when the probe's preflight accepts it (`--device mps`, no `--force`).\nThat is PyTorch on Metal; it says nothing about MLX LoRA.\n\n'''\ns=s[:old_start]+new+s[old_end:]\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\ncat /tmp/train-out5.log"

Release\ndocs/publishing.md:114:## Adding a GitHub Environment\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"OpenAI-compatible chat server for UniMedVL (issue #6).\n\nUniMedVL (https://github.com/uni-medical/UniMedVL, Apache-2.0) is a BAGEL\nmodel with its own Python package and its own ``model.chat`` call. Neither\nllama.cpp nor ``transformers.AutoModel`` can load it: there is no GGUF, and\nthe checkpoint's ``auto_map`` points to files that are not in the repository.\nThis server loads it the same way as upstream's\n``codes/interactive_vqa_inferencer.py`` and answers ``/v1/chat/completions``.\nmedbench can then score it with ``--backend openai``, like every other model.\n\nThe server is our own code and stays under the Unlicense. It imports the\nupstream checkout at run time and does not copy it. The checkout and the\nweights keep their Apache-2.0 terms (see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).\n\nRun it with the Python of the upstream environment (Python 3.10, torch 2.6.0,\ntransformers 4.49.0, accelerate 1.7.0 and flash-attn; see\n``scripts/medbench-model-run.sh``), from the root of a checkout at\n:data:`CODE_COMMIT`::\n\n    cd UniMedVL && python -I /path/to/unimedvl_server.py \\\\\n        --code-dir . --model-dir /path/to/checkpoint --port 8089\n\nEndpoints:\n\n* ``GET /health`` - 200 once the model is loaded;\n* ``GET /v1/models`` - the model name;\n* ``GET /metrics`` - versions, limits, load time, peak GPU memory and speed;\n* ``POST /v1/chat/completions`` - text parts and base64 ``data:`` images.\n\nThe server never downloads anything a request names. It answers one request\nat a time, because the GPU holds one model.\n\nFailures:\n\n* CUDA out-of-memory frees the cache and answers HTTP 507 with error type\n  ``out_of_memory``. The server stays up, so the next item can still run.\n* Any other model error answers HTTP 500 after the same cleanup.\n* Deadlines are kept by the caller: medbench's ``--request-timeout`` and\n  ``--time-budget``, and the workflow's ``timeout-minutes``. On exit,\n# Evaluation validity: what a medbench score can show\n\nThis page lists what we checked about the benchmark's labels, splits,\nsample sizes, scoring rules and sources. It also lists what we could not\ncheck. It answers [issue #7](https://github.com/konard/medical-neural-network-ml/issues/7).\n\nThe short version: the real teaching images and pages are a **smoke test**.\nThey show that a model can read real files and answer in a usable format.\nThey are far too few, and too easy, to rank models or support a clinical\nclaim. The labels were reviewed by the maintainers, **not by clinicians**.\n\n## Label review\n\n`src/medbench/data/label_review.json` has one entry for each of the 37 real\nimages and pages. You can print it with:\n\n```bash\nmedbench review                     # every task\nmedbench review --task imaging-xray # one task\n```\n\nEach entry records:\n\n| Field | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| `view` | Projection, sequence or plane, as stated by the source. Two X-rays are **AP**, not PA: on AP, heart and mediastinum look larger. The X-ray prompt no longer says every X-ray is frontal PA. |\n| `laterality` | The side of the finding and how it was read. Sides are the **patient's** side. On X-ray and MRI that is mirrored in the image (radiological convention). Ultrasound sides that the source does not state are not scored. |\n| `label_source` | Where the label comes from: the Commons uploader's description, the RxHandBD dataset's own label, or a proofread Wikisource transcription. |\n| `source_group` | Items that may share a patient, uploader or source. Splits keep a group together. |\n| `uncertainty` | Known doubts, e.g. \"projection not stated\", \"side cannot be checked from pixels\", \"only *mass* is scorable, not the histology\". |",

The gates on main catch what a stale merge breaks.\n\n## Trusted Publishing (#8) and Required Checks\n\nPyPI trusted publishing for `medical-neural-network-ml` is not configured\nyet (issue #8). The estimator uses 16.\n- LoRA rank 8 to 64 added 0.25 GB.\n- SmolVLM-256M used 1 088 image tokens per image with default splitting and 64 without.\n- Measured peaks were 0.62–0.84 of the estimate, because the estimate assumes bf16 plus 1.5 GB of GPU overhead.\n- The full fine-tune and the split-image run were killed by the watchdog above 2.3 GB, as their estimates predicted.\n\nLibraries used: torch, transformers, peft, accelerate and bitsandbytes (CUDA only); `psutil`-free `/proc` and `getrusage` sampling; `nvidia-smi`. Summary\n\nThis addresses the five open audit issues (#6–#10) tracked by #11. The code, workflows and documentation are done for all five. Three of them include steps this pull request cannot carry out, because they need hardware or account access that is not available here. Those steps are listed under each issue and in **What is not done**. They are not reported as passing.\n\nFixes #6\nFixes #7\nFixes #8\nFixes #9\nFixes #10\nFixes #11\n\n> **Closing caveat.** #6 still needs a dedicated-GPU run. #8 still needs the PyPI maintainer to register the trusted publisher. #10 still needs an admin to apply the rulesets. The `Fixes` lines are kept as #11 asked. If you would rather keep those issues open until the manual steps are done, remove their lines before merging.\n\n## Requirements, solutions and libraries per issue\n\n### #6: UniMedVL and MedGemma 27B on GPU hardware\n\n| Requirement | What this PR does |\n|---|---|\n| Pin UniMedVL code and checkpoint; adapter using its supported runtime; keep notices | `scripts/unimedvl_server.py` is an OpenAI-compatible server. It loads UniMedVL the way upstream's `interactive_vqa_inferencer.py` does, from code commit `f51aa0a` and checkpoint revision `29918ce`, with an isolated runtime in `scripts/unimedvl-requirements.txt`. medbench scores it with `--backend openai`. Our code stays under the Unlicense; the upstream code and weights keep Apache-2.0 in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. |\n| Run all seven tasks for both models | `scripts/medbench-model-run.sh` runs every task for `medgemma-27b` (GGUF and mmproj) and `unimedvl`. It keeps going when one item fails and reports completed/requested counts per task, with attribution. **Not run:** no GPU is available (see below). |\n| Versions, limits, peak GPU and host memory, disk, cold start, speed, wall time | `medbench monitor` and the server's `/metrics` record the GPU, driver, CUDA and runtime versions, context/image/output limits, peak GPU and host memory, free disk, load time, prompt/decode speed and wall time. |\n| OOM, deadline and cleanup; trusted manual dispatch only | CUDA OOM answers HTTP 507 and frees the cache, so the run continues. Deadlines come from `--request-timeout`, `--time-budget` and `timeout-minutes`. The GPU job runs only on `workflow_dispatch` from main, in the `gpu` environment, and deletes its downloads even after a failure. |\n| Raw reports; R8/R9/R12/R13 split into implemented, estimated and measured | `requirements.md` now separates these three. Reports upload as artifacts. |\n\nLibraries: llama.cpp serves MedGemma 27B GGUF. UniMedVL is a BAGEL model with no GGUF, and its `auto_map` points to files missing from the checkpoint, so neither llama.cpp nor `transformers.AutoModel` can load it. The adapter therefore wraps upstream's own inferencer.\n\n### #7: Labels, sampling and medical scoring\n\n| Requirement | What this PR does |\n|---|---|\n| Label, laterality, view, balance and overlap review with provenance | `src/medbench/data/label_review.json` covers all 37 real items and is printed by `medbench review`. Two X-rays are AP, so the prompt no longer says every X-ray is a frontal PA view. Reviewers are the maintainers, **not clinicians**, and `clinician_reviewed` stays `false`. |\n| Patient/source-separated splits and sample-size targets | `src/medbench/validity.py` provides grouped splits that keep each `source_group` together, plus sample-size targets. `docs/evaluation-validity.md` explains that the teaching set is a smoke test. |\n| Confidence intervals, invalid/abstention/truncation rates, coverage; DDXPlus parser on all 49 choices and adversarial outputs | Reports include Wilson intervals and answer-quality counters. `tests/test_medbench_ddxplus_parser.py` checks all 49 conditions and adversarial answers. |\n| Negation, dose/unit, OCR normalization, laterality scoring | `src/medbench/clinical_text.py` is a small NegEx-style subset that handles dose-unit parsing. It has example-based tests; these examples were not reviewed by a clinician. |\n| Source terms and attribution; Unlicense code; no \"all public domain\" claim | `docs/evaluation-validity.md` gives the source terms and provenance. |\n| Specialist baselines and evaluation libraries | The `ocr-baseline` CI job runs Tesseract and uploads its reports. PaddleOCR, TorchXRayVision, VLMEvalKit, lmms-eval, MultiMedEval, HealthBench and medspaCy/negspaCy are compared with checked licenses but not yet run. |\n\n### #8: PyPI trusted publishing\n\n| Requirement | What this PR does |\n|---|---|\n| Never publish to someone else's package | The distribution is `medical-neural-network-ml`. Nothing was uploaded and no PyPI setting was changed. |\n| Publisher setup (owner `konard`, repository `medical-neural-network-ml`, workflow `release.yml`, environment blank) | `docs/publishing.md` lists the exact settings and the first-release steps for the maintainer. |\n| Publish only after the real OIDC exchange succeeds | The preflight still performs the real exchange. On pull requests it runs in report mode and annotates the missing publisher. **On main it fails on purpose** with `release-preflight: refusing to release` and the settings to enter. It is not turned into a pass. |\n| Verify license expression, license files, manifest, entrypoint, install smoke test and release | `scripts/check_distribution.py` checks the wheel and sdist before any upload: PEP 639 expression and files, manifest against `src/`, `RECORD`, the `medbench` entrypoint and an offline install. The sdist no longer includes CI logs or experiments. The post-release check of the GitHub release is listed in the docs, as it needs a real release. |\n\nLibraries used: `build`, `twine check` and `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` (OIDC).\n\n### #9: Calibrating hardware and training estimates\n\n| Requirement | What this PR does |\n|---|---|\n| Support matrix | `src/medbench/support.py` / `medbench support` lists models × runtimes × formats × tasks. |\n| Measure inference and full/LoRA/QLoRA peaks at explicit settings, covering vision activations, dequantization, fragmentation, loading peak, and checkpoint and optimizer disk | `scripts/measure_training_memory.py` runs a real training step and records loading, step and checkpoint peaks, optimizer state, image tokens and (on CUDA) reserved versus allocated memory. It checks memory before allocating and compares the result with the estimate. The kernel's peak counter is restarted after loading, so the step peak is its own. |\n| 4B on the M3 Pro only when the preflight allows | Documented as `--device mps` without `--force`. PyTorch Metal is not MLX, and the docs say so. **Not run here** (no Mac). |\n| 27B and UniMedVL on dedicated GPUs; MLX not inferred from CUDA NF4 | The commands are in `docs/hardware-workflows.md`. QLoRA is refused off CUDA, as \"unsupported\", with no MLX inference. **Not run** (no GPU). |\n| GPU efficiency, image tokens, KV allocation, concurrency, communication | `medbench estimate` takes `--ctx-size`, `--parallel`, `--gpus` and `--scaling-efficiency` (default 80 %, range 60–95 %). The logits term is now counted. |\n| Peak resources of every workflow | Each heavy step runs under `medbench monitor` and uploads a `resources-*` report. The measured peaks of all seven workflows on `165a710` are in `docs/hardware-workflows.md` and `docs/case-studies/issue-1/data/ci-resources-20261016/`. The heaviest is the MedGemma 4B CPU smoke test: 5.74 of 16.8 GB host memory, llama-server at 4.71 GB RSS. |\n| Dated prices, uncertainty ranges, labelled hypotheses | Prices are dated or labelled as examples. Estimates carry ranges. The \"27B QLoRA fits one 24 GB GPU\" claim is now a labelled hypothesis: by formula it needs 28 GB at 2 048 tokens. |\n\n**Measured on a CPU** (6-core EPYC, fp32, 3.1 GB limit, RSS watchdog at 2.3 GB; `docs/case-studies/issue-1/data/training-memory-cpu-20261016/`):\n\n- From 256 to 1 024 tokens the SmolLM2-135M step peak grew by 0.68–0.70 GB, about 18–19 bytes per token and vocabulary entry. The estimator uses 16.\n- LoRA rank 8 to 64 added 0.25 GB.\n- SmolVLM-256M used 1 088 image tokens per image with default splitting and 64 without.\n- Measured peaks were 0.62–0.84 of the estimate, because the estimate assumes bf16 plus 1.5 GB of GPU overhead.\n- The full fine-tune and the split-image run were killed by the watchdog above 2.3 GB, as their estimates predicted.\n\nLibraries used: torch, transformers, peft, accelerate and bitsandbytes (CUDA only); `/proc`, `vm_stat` and `getrusage` sampling without extra dependencies; `nvidia-smi`. Related tools: HF `accelerate estimate-memory` (weights only), PyTorch's memory snapshot, and MLX `mx.metal.get_peak_memory`.\n\n### #10: Branch protection and immutable Action pins\n\n| Requirement | What this PR does |\n|---|---|\n| Required checks, review, narrow release-bot bypass; test contributor PRs and the version commit | The rulesets live in `.github/rulesets/`. They require three uniquely named gates: `Pipeline Status (CI/CD)`, `(Compatibility)` and `(Security)`. Compatibility now runs on every pull request so it can be required. `docs/repository-policy.md` has the bypass and a five-step test plan. `scripts/repository_rulesets.py` checks or applies the rulesets; it applies only with `--yes`. **The rulesets were not applied to the live repository.** |\n| SHA-pinned Actions with version comments; automated update PRs | Every action is pinned to a commit with its release in a comment. Dependabot updates actions and pip weekly with a seven-day cooldown. zizmor and actionlint run in CI. |\n| Least-privilege tokens, no persisted credentials, fork PRs | Permissions are set per job, and `persist-credentials: false` is used except for the release writer, which is justified in the docs. Fork behavior is documented. |\n| Self-hosted GPU runner policy | The GPU job runs on trusted manual dispatch only, in the `gpu` environment, with cleanup. The documented policy requires ephemeral, isolated runners before any GPU host is attached. |\n| How #8 affects required checks; no masking | Covered in \"Trusted Publishing (#8) and Required Checks\": green on pull requests, intentionally red on main until the publisher exists. |\n\n## What is not done (needs hardware or account access)\n\n- **#6 / #9 GPU runs:** no GPU was provisioned. MedGemma 27B, UniMedVL and 4B/27B training must be measured by dispatching the GPU job, or by running the documented commands on a dedicated card.\n- **#9 M3 Pro:** the training probe has not run on Apple silicon.\n- **#8:** a maintainer has to register the PyPI trusted publisher. Until then the CI/CD preflight on main fails with the instructions; it passes in report mode on pull requests.\n- **#10:** an admin has to run `scripts/repository_rulesets.py apply --yes` after reading `docs/repository-policy.md`. The `Branch Rulesets` check warns on pull requests and fails on main until then.\n- **#7:** the label review is not clinician-reviewed, and the external baselines and libraries have not been run.\n- **Dependency Review:** it comments on transformers 4.49.0 advisories in `scripts/unimedvl-requirements.txt`. UniMedVL's upstream pins transformers 4.49.0, so these advisories are accepted with reasons, and only their GHSA IDs are allowed. The check passes.\n\n## Tests\n\nRun locally on the final commit, all passing:\n\n- `ruff check .` and `ruff format --check .`\n- `mypy src/`\n- `python scripts/check_file_size.py`\n- `bash
